1be7a86946328a3c: TOKYO: Japan's Nikkei share average snapped a six-session losing streak on Friday as artificial intelligence-related shares rebounded, although gains were limited by caution ahead of corporate earnings reports and US midterm elections.
The Nikkei rose 1.39 per cent to 65,324.29 after a near five per cent drop in the previous session. The index fell 5.37 per cent for the week.
The broader Topix rose 1.67 per cent to 4,066 but fell 0.95 per cent for the week.

"The shares rebounded as investors bought back stocks after sharp losses in the previous session... there were no other factors for the gains," said Daisuke Hashizume, senior strategist at Daiwa Securities.
"Market players see little reason to buy shares aggressively ahead of the release of corporate earnings and the US midterm elections next month."
Markets are watching whether the election outcome will affect US President Donald Trump's proposals for US$5,000 payouts for US adults and higher military spending, said Hashizume.
In Japan, chip-making equipment maker Tokyo Electron rose 2.56 per cent, memory chip maker Kioxia gained 3.84 per cent and technology investor SoftBank Group rose 1.9 per cent.
Chip-testing equipment maker Advantest recouped early losses to end 0.55 per cent higher.
BayCurrent surged 17.25 per cent to become the top percentage gainer on the Nikkei after the consulting firm said it would use excess cash for investments and share buybacks.
Banks supported the Topix, with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group and Mizuho Financial Group rising 1.82 per cent and 1.72 per cent, respectively.
Of more than 1,500 stocks trading on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's prime market, 83 per cent rose, 14 per cent fell and two per cent traded flat.
3d92d66638245ea9: TOKYO, Oct 16 — Imagine your phone suddenly blaring a warning that a catastrophic magnitude 9.9 earthquake is about to strike.

That’s exactly the sort of alarm that sounded across parts of Japan this afternoon, when the country’s sophisticated earthquake early warning system mistakenly forecast one of the most powerful tremors in recorded history.
The only problem? The earthquake was nowhere near as powerful as predicted.
The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) issued an emergency alert at 12.40pm local time, warning of potentially violent shaking across northern, eastern and central Japan.
But just eight minutes later, the warning was withdrawn after officials discovered that their system had dramatically overestimated the earthquake’s magnitude.
The actual quake, which struck off Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula, measured magnitude 6.9 — a substantial earthquake in its own right, but far weaker than the monster tremor initially forecast.
And while the warning suggested that parts of Japan could experience devastating shaking, the strongest tremors recorded in the country barely registered.
A megaquake that wasn’t

According to The Japan Times, the earthquake struck at a depth of about 160km, but the JMA’s automated system mistakenly located its epicentre near the Kuril Islands, between Japan’s Hokkaido and Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula.
The error led to an extraordinary magnitude 9.9 estimate, with the agency initially predicting shaking reaching the maximum level of 7 on Japan’s seismic intensity scale.
In reality, the strongest shaking recorded in Japan was just 1 on the scale, including in Hakodate, Hokkaido, where the tremor was barely perceptible.
No tsunami warnings or advisories were issued.
At a press briefing, a JMA spokesman acknowledged that the system had incorrectly calculated both the earthquake’s magnitude and location.
Officials also ruled out a cyberattack, saying they were investigating what had caused the dramatic miscalculation.
“We are currently investigating the cause and will provide an explanation as soon as it is determined,” the spokesman said.
Just how extraordinary was the initial estimate?
A magnitude 9.9 earthquake would be considerably stronger than the largest earthquake ever instrumentally recorded — the magnitude 9.5 tremor that devastated Chile in 1960.
It would also dwarf the magnitude 9.0 earthquake that struck northeastern Japan on March 11, 2011, unleashing a deadly tsunami and triggering the Fukushima nuclear disaster.
When every second counts
For a country accustomed to living with earthquakes, Japan’s early warning system is a crucial part of everyday disaster preparedness.
Introduced to the public in 2007, the system is designed to give people a few precious seconds to protect themselves before potentially destructive shaking reaches them.

It works by detecting the first, faster-moving seismic waves produced by an earthquake and using that information to estimate where the quake occurred, how powerful it is and where strong shaking is likely to strike.
Alerts can then be sent to mobile phones, television stations and public speakers, while trains and other infrastructure can take emergency precautions.
But there is a catch.
Because the system must make those calculations almost instantaneously, it relies on preliminary data that can sometimes produce inaccurate estimates.
Today’s incident demonstrated just how dramatic such an error can be, with a magnitude 6.9 earthquake initially mistaken for a potentially record-breaking 9.9 event.
Fortunately, the warning was withdrawn within minutes, with no significant shaking recorded in Japan.
For the JMA, however, the question remains: how did a system built to give people a vital head start in an earthquake get this one so spectacularly wrong?

f6e1439597ec568f: KOTA BARU: The Kelantan Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) is conducting further investigations to determine whether other parties were involved in the misappropriation of subsidised cooking oil, following the seizure of 4,127 kilogrammes of the controlled item in Kampung Chetok, Pasir Mas, yesterday.
Kelantan KPDN director Hanif Yusabra Yusuf said the investigation aims to uncover potential illicit activities involving the misappropriation of subsidised controlled goods.
During the operation part of 'Ops Tiris 4.0 (Integrated) carried out at 8
pm, the Kelantan KPDN seized subsidised cooking oil valued at RM11,053.50, along with five vehicles, bringing the total value of the seizure to RM138,053.50.

"The operation, conducted by Kelantan KPDN's Intelligence and Special Action Unit (URTK) in collaboration with the Patrol Unit (MPV) of the Pasir Mas district police headquarters, resulted in two separate cases.

"The first case involved the seizure of 1,577 kilogrammes of subsidised cooking oil of various brands, along with a Toyota Unser, a Mitsubishi Pajero, and a Nissan Navara, with a total value of RM70,678.50," he said during a press conference at the Kelantan KPDN headquarters here today.
According to him, the second case involved the seizure of 2,550 kilogrammes of subsidised cooking oil, along with a Toyota Hiace and a Mitsubishi Pajero, with a total value of RM67,375.
"The seized cooking oil consisted of one-kilogramme packets of various brands, as well as five-kilogramme bottled cooking oil produced by local companies in Kelantan and other states."

"Previously, the act of gathering supplies of subsidised cooking oil from wholesalers and storing them at specific locations is believed to have been the modus operandi of the parties involved," he said.
Hanif said action has also been taken against individuals linked to both cases.
The cases are being investigated under Sections 21 and 20(1) of the Control of Supplies Act 1961, as well as Regulation 3(1) of the Control of Supplies Regulations 1974.

These provisions relate to the possession of controlled goods with the intent to commit an offence, the unauthorised transfer of controlled goods to unlicensed premises, and the wholesale of controlled goods without a valid license.

He added that the Kelantan branch of the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) will continue to intensify enforcement operations particularly in border areas to curb the misappropriation and smuggling of subsidised controlled goods, and to ensure that these supplies are not misused. — BERNAMA
ac2572c1e1f75ba5: NEW DELHI, Oct 16 — Authorities closed a central New Delhi park today before a fresh protest seeking the removal of India’s election chief over a voter-roll revision that critics say has disenfranchised millions.
Organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), the campaign has become the focal point of opposition anger over allegations that the revised rolls favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party.
The Election Commission of India, which oversees voting in the world’s most populous nation, has denied any wrongdoing.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke urged supporters to rally at the capital’s Central Park after two of his colleagues were detained for breaching security barricades at Jantar Mantar, where they had gone to wave the national flag.
Earlier this week, police removed authorisation for Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site.
Today, thousands of security personnel were deployed in parts of the city, with yellow-coloured metal barricades put up at key intersections.
Dipke said he was undeterred despite the possibility of being arrested ahead of Friday’s protest.
“Why are you so afraid of cockroaches?” Dipke said.
“I want to tell Narendra Modi that we are not afraid... if waving the Indian national flag lands you in jail, we are ready,” he said Thursday.
Delhi’s municipal authorities said they were closing the Central Park for two days for “administrative” reasons.
Delhi Police have barred public gatherings around Connaught Place citing concerns about public order and safety.
Violation of the orders would “attract suitable legal action”, police said Thursday, but added that they would allow “selected persons” to gather at a “suitable place”.
In recent days, the Indian capital has seen street protests over a large-scale voter roll revision exercise overseen by chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
More than 130 million names have been removed from electoral lists under the revision exercise, according to media reports.
Critics say the removals have disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims.
Election authorities say the move was intended to eliminate duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries.

Members of Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh dismissed the allegations, saying the sole agenda of the opposition parties was “to destroy democratic institutions and create unrest in the country”.
“Their fight is not for electoral reform... not for Gyanesh Kumar, not for the bright future of the country’s youth,” he said at a news conference.
“Rather, this is their conspiracy to seize power by creating anarchy in the country.” — AFP

c3e7caca6df1b877: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian diving has lost the plot after a series of wrong decisions, and the sport's future looks bleak despite Malaysia Aquatics (MAS) identifying areas for improvement ahead of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
To hail Malaysia's Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games campaign as a success after winning one silver and two bronzes, against a target of one bronze, is pathetic and unacceptable.
The results were nothing to shout about for a nation that was once Asia's second-best diving power behind China.
Instead, Malaysia finished fourth in the diving medal standings, behind champions China (10-4-2), South Korea (0-2-3) and Japan (0-2-2).
There was a time when Malaysia produced a world champion and Olympic medallists.
Today, Malaysian divers are struggling even at Asian level.

MAS diving technical director Yeoh Ken Nee said greater difficulty, sharper execution and consistency would be crucial ahead of next year's World Aquatics Championships in Budapest, which will run from June 26-July 18.
"Our next major target is the Olympic qualification for LA28, and the qualification period is already approaching quickly," said Ken Nee.
"We have around eight months to prepare, so it will be a challenging period for the divers and the coaching team."
The World Championships will open the Olympic qualification pathway, with top-eight finishes in individual events offering an early route to LA28.
Ken Nee admitted that Malaysia must improve further in the individual events, particularly on the platform, to compete with the leading nations.
"Our divers need to perform more dynamic and stronger dives, with higher difficulty and better execution," he said.
"These are the areas we need to focus on if we want to score higher and close the gap with the leading countries internationally."
Ken Nee said the focus must now shift towards raising the divers' competitive level.
China remain the benchmark, but he stressed that Malaysia's priority was to improve their own performances.
"Our focus now is not just on comparing ourselves with China. We need to continue raising the standard of our own divers, particularly in difficulty, execution and consistency," he said.
Ken Nee also sees promise in the synchro events, provided the divers can minimise mistakes.
"When our divers can execute their dives consistently with minimum mistakes, we can be competitive and challenge for medals," he added.
LA28 will offer 136 diving places across eight events, comprising four individual and four synchronised disciplines.
After Budapest, the qualification pathway will continue through continental competitions before concluding with the first two Diving World Cup stops in 2028.
Those World Cup meets will determine the synchro qualifiers, with hosts the United States receiving automatic places.
They will also provide further opportunities to qualify in the individual events.
For Malaysia, Budapest offers the first chance to secure individual berths, while the pairs must build towards their decisive qualifying tests in 2028.

d6e5e468f099e230: OCT 16 — The United States has long portrayed itself as the world’s most enduring constitutional democracy.
Yet beneath its impressive economic, military and technological achievements lies a society increasingly divided by inequality, political polarisation and declining confidence in its institutions.
In his ambitious and provocative book on the possibility of a Second American Revolution, Datuk Lee Boon Chye offers a penetrating examination of these contradictions.
The exact title is “The Creative Destruction of The American Democracy: Trump 2.0 and the 2nd American Revolution,” published under the VinLin Press.
Lee’s central argument is that America’s political institutions, once responsible for its extraordinary rise, have become increasingly incapable of correcting their own structural weaknesses.
This is not merely another criticism of President Donald Trump. Indeed, one of the book’s principal strengths is its refusal to treat Trump as the original cause of America’s democratic malaise.

Instead, Lee argues that Trump’s political resurgence reflects decades of accumulated grievances involving stagnant wages, widening wealth inequality, declining social mobility and the growing influence of wealthy elites over public policy.
The distinction is fundamental. Trump did not create these contradictions. He exploited them.
Across 18 chapters, Lee constructs a sweeping argument that connects America’s contemporary political turbulence with the philosophical foundations of its republic.
His examination begins with Trump’s electoral victories in 2016 and 2024, before proceeding to the deeper socioeconomic conditions that made such political upheavals possible.
Lee is particularly persuasive when explaining how economic growth and corporate profitability have increasingly become disconnected from the living standards of ordinary Americans.
While productivity and financial markets have expanded substantially, many working-class households have struggled to experience corresponding improvements in their purchasing power.
This contradiction exposes the limitations of neoliberal capitalism, particularly the assumption that economic prosperity automatically translates into broadly distributed social benefits.

Lee traces these developments to the economic doctrines associated with Ronald Reagan and Milton Friedman, arguing that shareholder primacy, globalisation and declining labour bargaining power have progressively weakened the American middle class.
The book subsequently examines healthcare inequality, opioid addiction, mass incarceration, gun violence, homelessness, suicide and unequal educational opportunities.

These are not treated as isolated social problems. Rather, Lee presents them as interconnected manifestations of an economic and political order increasingly unable to reconcile private prosperity with collective welfare.
His discussion of healthcare is especially revealing.
Despite enormous expenditure, the United States continues to experience serious disparities in medical access and health outcomes.
For Lee, this demonstrates how market mechanisms cannot invariably substitute for effective public governance.
Equally important is his examination of the American criminal justice system, including the controversies surrounding Jeffrey Epstein.
The broader issue is not simply individual wrongdoing but whether wealth and political connections permit influential individuals to enjoy privileges unavailable to ordinary citizens.
Nevertheless, some allegations and interpretations surrounding Epstein would benefit from more rigorous differentiation between established evidence, disputed claims and speculation.
The book becomes intellectually more ambitious when Lee revisits the American Revolution and the philosophical contributions of Thomas Hobbes, John Locke, Jean-Jacques Rousseau and Montesquieu.
Here, he challenges the assumption that America’s founding constitutional arrangements remain universally applicable regardless of changing historical circumstances.
His argument is that constitutional durability can become constitutional rigidity.

The Electoral College, entrenched two-party competition, expensive electoral campaigns and formidable barriers to constitutional amendment have collectively restricted meaningful institutional renewal.
Consequently, American democracy risks becoming procedurally competitive without being substantively responsive.
This is perhaps the book’s most consequential observation.
Democratic legitimacy cannot depend exclusively on periodic elections. It must also rest upon institutions capable of translating public preferences into effective governance.
Lee further examines the contradictions between America’s founding ideals and its historical conduct, particularly slavery, Indigenous dispossession, racial segregation and foreign intervention.

These contradictions deserve serious reflection, although his critique of Enlightenment philosophy occasionally understates the capacity of liberal constitutionalism for gradual reform and self-correction.
The book’s concluding proposition is especially provocative: America may ultimately require a Second Revolution, potentially involving the replacement of its existing Constitution.
This conclusion is intellectually stimulating but remains debatable.
Institutional rigidity does not necessarily make revolutionary rupture inevitable.
Constitutional interpretation, electoral reform, civic mobilisation and political realignment can also generate substantial transformation.

Indeed, the historical resilience of American institutions suggests that the relationship between constitutional continuity and democratic renewal is more complicated than a choice between preservation and revolution.
For readers in Malaysia and Asean, however, Lee’s analysis carries significance beyond American domestic politics.

In his ambitious and provocative book on the possibility of a Second American Revolution, Datuk Lee Boon Chye offers a penetrating examination of these contradictions.

A United States weakened by internal divisions may become more unpredictable internationally, alternating between strategic retrenchment, economic nationalism and assertive demonstrations of military power.
Asean cannot assume that American institutional stability will indefinitely guarantee strategic consistency.
Nor should Southeast Asian countries conclude that China’s rise automatically resolves the uncertainties arising from American political dysfunction.
The region must instead cultivate greater strategic autonomy, strengthen its economic resilience and maintain diplomatic engagement with all major powers.

Lee’s book therefore deserves attention not because its prediction of revolutionary transformation is necessarily correct, but because it identifies the accumulating contradictions that make such a proposition conceivable.
Its breadth occasionally comes at the expense of analytical precision, and several sweeping arguments warrant greater qualification.
Nevertheless, its willingness to connect political economy, constitutional philosophy and social deterioration is commendable.
Ultimately, the book reminds readers that great powers seldom decline solely because of external competitors.
They become vulnerable when their institutions lose the capacity to address the grievances of their own citizens.
Whether America experiences a Second Revolution remains uncertain.
What is increasingly difficult to dismiss is Lee Boon Chye’s underlying warning: a democracy that cannot renew itself risks becoming a prisoner of the very institutions that once made it successful.
* Phar Kim Beng is professor of Asean Studies, and director at the Institute of International and Asean Studies, International Islamic University Malaysia.

afacfde94b5ae9fe: SINGAPORE: Malaysia-born actor Jaspers Lai has turned his frustration over the ongoing haze into a parody song that has amused social media users, with his video garnering more than 1.2 million views.
The 39-year-old shared the video on Instagram on Oct 10, slipping into his popular Auntie Guci persona in a maroon long-sleeved top and pearl necklace.
He used a smoke filter to recreate the haze while lip-syncing to a parody of Malaysian singer Jess Lee's hit breakup ballad A, B, C, D.
In the caption, Lai tagged Jess and asked: "Not even a single sorry?"
He also appealed to the singer: "Can you sing this version? Sing the haze away please."
According to a news report, Lai spent an entire evening rewriting the lyrics and used artificial intelligence to produce the track.
The reworked version pokes fun at the haze, describing irritated eyes, persistent coughing and the seemingly endless smoke-filled air.

Lai also injected humour into the everyday frustrations caused by the poor air quality, joking that his boss still expected him to turn up for work and that he could not afford to obtain a medical certificate.
Taking a swipe at the cross-border haze, he sings: "You and I are neighbours, how can you bear to turn my home into Genting?"
The line compares the smoke-covered surroundings to Malaysia's famous hill resort, known for its cool, misty weather.
The video attracted more than 40,000 likes and drew reactions from fellow celebrities, including actor Romeo Tan, who asked: "Is your house still okay?"
Lai responded cheekily: "Can I move in with you for a week?"
Tan played along, saying he could even stay for a year.
Lai followed up with another parody video on Oct 13, this time dressed in a school uniform and joking about students getting a break from classes because of the poor air quality.
Working adults, however, were not as fortunate.
"But you still need to go to work! Haha! A song a day to chase the haze away!" he wrote.
e8870fbadfd08877: SINGAPORE: PetroChina is preparing to restart a mothballed crude oil processing unit in northeast China next month to replenish domestic fuel stocks until a replacement refinery is constructed, according to multiple industry and trade sources.

In July 2025, PetroChina, the listed arm of CNPC, shuttered the entire 410,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Dalian Petrochemical refinery, once the group's largest and most profitable, in line with Beijing's efforts to cut excess refining capacity and focus on producing higher value petrochemicals.

PetroChina previously planned to restart a 200,000 bpd crude distillation unit (CDU) at Dalian in mid-2026, but the plan was held back as the US-Israeli war with Iran disrupted crude supplies and sent prices surging.

The plan to restart the CDU gained traction in recent months as China has faced depleted crude and fuel stocks after months of reduced crude imports and refining output because of the supply disruptions.

The monthly crude feed for the restarted CDU is planned at 500,000 to 600,000 metric tons, said one of the sources, a person with direct knowledge of the matter. That is equal to about 122,000 to 146,000 bpd, or about two per cent of China's seaborne crude imports in September, and translates to an operating rate of roughly 61 per cent to 73 per cent of total processing capacity for the unit.
The refinery is expected to receive crude shipments from South America and the Middle East next week for the restart, said one of the trade sources, who was briefed on the restart process.

Another factor behind restarting the old Dalian plant is a delay in the planned startup of a US$10 billion new refinery complex under construction on a nearby island, said two of the sources, traders who were also briefed on the company's plans. The new site was expected to start in mid-2028, they said.

The startup of the new complex is expected in March 2029, according to a September 8 tender document reviewed by Reuters from state-owned pipeline operator PipeChina seeking technical services for pipe works related to the restart of the old Dalian refinery.
PetroChina did not immediately respond to a request for comment sent by email.

32da615df7719857: YEREVAN (Armenia): UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Thursday launched the first global assessment report on the implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, warning that global efforts remain off track to meet the 2030 targets despite widespread national commitments.

The State of Biodiversity Action report, released in the Armenian capital of Yerevan ahead of the 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), evaluates collective progress under the landmark framework adopted in December 2022, which sets out 23 targets to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030 and four long-term goals for 2050.

According to the report, nearly 90 per cent of the CBD's 196 Parties have established national biodiversity targets, close to 60 per cent have developed national biodiversity strategies and action plans, and over 70 per cent have submitted national reports.
Indigenous peoples and local communities, subnational governments, businesses and civil society organisations have also registered around 5,000 commitments.
However, such widespread engagement has not yet translated into sufficient progress.
None of the 23 global targets presents a fully positive picture, and fewer than half of the national targets assessed by Parties are currently on track, the report found.
While national targets address an average of 22 of the 23 global targets, many fail to cover their full scope.

For instance, far fewer countries have committed to reducing harmful subsidies under Target 18 than promoting positive incentives, and current national pledges under Target 3 fall well short of the goal to conserve 30 per cent of land and sea by 2030.
The report identified gaps in financing and other means of implementation, whole-of-government and whole-of-society action, as well as data and knowledge needed to track progress.
Targets requiring action beyond environment ministries — including business action, sustainable consumption, harmful incentives and finance — are among those lagging furthest behind.
"The report shows that many of the critical elements of progress, including finance, capacity, cooperation and data, are still missing in action," Guterres said.

The UN chief called for greater financial and technical support, particularly for developing countries, the reform of harmful subsidies, nature-positive investment, and stronger integration of biodiversity across public policies and budgets.

"The very biodiversity we depend on needs tangible progress, not more promises," Inger Andersen, executive director of the UN Environment Programme, said in the report's foreword, urging immediate action to overcome implementation challenges.
The report will inform the first global review of collective progress under the framework at COP17, scheduled for Oct 19 through 30 in Yerevan. — BERNAMA
7ed4456d30fe1e48: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Heavy rain in Singapore yesterday morning failed to ease concerns over the haze, with some residents reporting blackish-grey rainwater collected in buckets outside their homes.
AsiaOne reported that a resident from Ang Mo Kio, identified only by her surname Zhong, had collected three buckets of rainwater that appeared blackish-grey.
A video shared on the Singapore Parents Instagram page also showed several buckets of murky rainwater, prompting concern among netizens.

According to a CNA video, raindrops can draw pollution particles out of the air as they fall. However, as haze contains fine smoke and pollution particles, rainfall may not remove them all quickly, resulting in discoloured rainwater.
Some social media users expressed concern over the possible health effects, with one saying they felt sorry for their lungs, according to the report.
Another said the water in their home fish pond had turned a similar colour.
Singapore’s air quality entered the very unhealthy range on Wednesday, with the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) reaching 203 in the western part of the island, AsiaOne reported.
Although air quality improved slightly earlier on Thursday, it deteriorated again, with readings reaching 205 micrograms per cubic metre in the central region at 5pm.
Sport Singapore has temporarily closed outdoor and non-air-conditioned ActiveSG facilities as a precautionary measure.
Eligible Singaporeans can also collect a pair of N95 masks, with details on eligibility, collection points and mask availability provided through the HazeMaskGoWhere website.
9b95afb4ae50b3c0: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuching City recorded a historic first point in Group H of the Asian Champions League Two (ACL2) after holding Hong Kong heavyweights Kitchee SC to a 1-1 draw at the Taha Ariffin Stadium on Thursday.
The result lifted the Kuching side to third place in the group, trailing second-placed Kitchee by a point.
On paper, the difference in resources was noticeable.

Kitchee fielded former Spain international Asier Illarramendi, a 2014 UEFA Champions League winner once signed by Real Madrid for €32.2 million (RM158 million), alongside former Cardiff City and Real Betis playmaker Víctor Camarasa.
However, Aidil Sharin Sahak's men were not intimidated, dictating the tempo and creating more chances than their expensively assembled opponents over 90 minutes.
"When it comes to the ACL, opponents have the financial power to sign unlimited top-tier foreign quality, like having an ex-Real Madrid player in their engine room," said Aidil.
"That level of experience definitely helps them. But talking strictly about football, today (yesterday) you could see that possession-wise and game-wise, we were superior.
"If you look at the statistics and the chances created, we had more than them. Quality-wise and performance-wise, we were right there."
Kuching City took an early lead in the second minute through an own goal by Kitchee goalkeeper Pong Cheuk Hei, but Everton Camargo equalised in the 14th minute.
Aidil said the difference between securing one point and all three came down to opposing goalkeeper heroics and clinical execution in the final third.
"We had very good chances to score, but unfortunately their keeper saved a few," he said.
"Although he fumbled the first goal, in the second half he pulled off crucial saves for Kitchee — at least two that were easily going in.
"The difference between the two teams was experience. Kitchee play every year in international competitions, and most of their squad are seasoned internationals."
Aidil stressed that tactical execution must eventually translate into wins, though he acknowledged squad depth remains a balancing act.
"We can compete, but we don't have luxury depth. We don't have two Ronald Ngahs or duplicate match-winners," he said.
"When you rotate, there is a risk of losing momentum, but these boys proved that with the right tactical application, we can go toe-to-toe with the best."
Kuching travel to South Korea next to take on Gangwon FC on Oct 29 in their third Group H match.
e7fa5bb99f4dd06d: SEOUL, Oct 16 — WINNER star Mino faces another 102 days of mandatory social service — nearly two years after completing his original stint — despite avoiding jail over a scandal involving repeated unauthorised absences.
The 33-year-old K-pop rapper, whose real name is Song Min-ho, could be called back to duty after his suspended prison sentence for violating South Korea’s Military Service Act became final.
South Korea’s Military Manpower Administration (MMA) is now reviewing the procedures for his return, according to Sports Chosun, citing a report by Star News today.
An MMA official told Star News that the relevant department was reviewing the process following the finalisation of the court ruling.
The agency had previously made clear that Mino would have to make up the 102 days he was found to have missed without a legitimate reason.
Mino was sentenced to one year in prison, suspended for two years, by the Seoul Western District Court on October 1 after being found guilty of repeatedly failing to report for duty.
He did not appeal within the seven-day deadline, leaving the ruling against him final.
However, an official who supervised his service and was convicted in connection with the case has appealed.
Mino served as a social service worker at facilities in Seoul’s Mapo district between March 2023 and December 2024, before being discharged on December 23, 2024.
The court heard that he had been absent without permission for 102 days during that period, amounting to nearly a quarter of the approximately 430 working days he was required to complete.
In one particularly striking example, Mino attended work for just four of the 23 required days in July 2024, missing the other 19.

The revelations sparked controversy in South Korea, where military service is compulsory for most able-bodied men and allegations of special treatment for celebrities frequently attract public scrutiny.
Mino had been assigned to alternative service rather than active military duty, working at the Mapo District Facilities Management Corporation and a community welfare facility.
Questions about his attendance first emerged towards the end of his service in December 2024, prompting an investigation by the authorities.
Prosecutors subsequently brought charges against Mino, alleging that he had repeatedly neglected his duties without justification.
During sentencing, the court stressed that military service was a fundamental obligation and that celebrities were no exception.
However, the judge took into account Mino’s admission of guilt, expressions of remorse and health circumstances in deciding to suspend his prison sentence.
Mino apologised in court, telling the judge: “As a South Korean youth, I failed to faithfully fulfil the national defence duty I must perform.”
He also expressed his desire to recover his health and complete his outstanding obligations if given another opportunity to serve.
On October 9, the rapper issued a handwritten apology on social media, acknowledging his actions and expressing regret over the controversy.
“Every day was filled with regret. My irresponsible past choices were shameful and hateful,” he wrote.
“I will not avoid my foolish mistakes and will reflect on them.”
He also pledged: “I will faithfully carry out the remaining procedures and obligations.”
Mino made his debut with YG Entertainment’s boy band WINNER in 2014, alongside Kang Seung-yoon, Kim Jin-woo, Lee Seung-hoon and former member Nam Tae-hyun.
The group went on to become one of K-pop’s most recognisable acts, with hits including Empty, Really Really and Love Me Love Me.
Beyond his work with WINNER, Mino has established a solo music career and built a following through appearances on popular South Korean variety programmes, including New Journey to the West.
His military service controversy has since overshadowed his entertainment career, with the latest development raising fresh questions about when he will be able to put the case behind him.
Although authorities are reviewing the procedures for his return to service, no official date or placement has been announced.
861ae66dce50090a: TIANJIN, Oct 16 — China has agreed in principle to Malaysia’s proposal to establish a World Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Council, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

Ahmad Zahid said the agreement which includes a proposal for China to serve as the permanent host was conveyed by his counterpart, Ding Xuexiang, and Minister of Education Huai Jinpeng during a meeting yesterday.

He noted that the proposal to establish the World TVET Council, with China acting as the permanent secretariat, was formally presented during his keynote address at the World Technical and Vocational Education and Training Development Conference 2026 (WVTEDC 2026) here today.

“I proposed it yesterday, and today I have officially put it forward in my speech. In terms of principle, Deputy Prime Minister Ding and China’s Minister of Education have agreed,” he said during a press conference following the event.

Ahmad Zahid, who also serves as the Minister of Rural and Regional Development, emphasised that the council is essential for creating a sustainable global platform to foster cooperation in skills development, technology, and workforce training, also expressed confidence in the initiative’s viability, citing China’s experience in organising TVET conferences over the past four years.

Ahmad Zahid, who also chairs the National TVET Committee, added that under this proposal, China would serve as the permanent secretariat to coordinate the sharing of knowledge and expertise within the TVET education ecosystem, thereby enabling member nations to benefit from ongoing collaboration.

The Deputy Prime Minister said the initiative also holds the potential to expand cooperation between TVET institutions in Malaysia and China including a proposed collaboration involving China’s “Luban Workshop” training centers, the Malaysia-China Institute (MCI), and various local TVET institutions.

Ahmad Zahid noted that such cooperation could pave the way for the implementation of skills training programmes, supporting Malaysia’s efforts to develop a highly skilled workforce capable of meeting the demands of the job market.
He added that the participation of over 100 countries and the attendance of 48 ministers at the WVTEDC 2026 conference reflect a global commitment to the development of education and skills training.

“We hope that efforts to strengthen the nation’s TVET ecosystem will continue to receive support from all stakeholders, in line with our aspiration to produce a workforce that meets industry needs, as Malaysia strives to become a highly skilled nation,” he said. — Bernama
060f6f849548bead: PEKAN: Two minors pleaded guilty in the magistrate's court here today to raping a 14-year-old girl earlier this month.
The duo entered their pleas after the charges were read to them separately by a court interpreter before magistrate Melody Woon Sze Mun.
They were charged with raping the victim in a hut in Kuala Pahang here between 9pm and 10pm on Oct 6.
Both were charged under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Siti Sarah Aqilah Lokman prosecuted, while both accused were represented by National Legal Aid Foundation counsel Noor Shuhada Arifin.
Woon set bail at RM8,000 for each accused and fixed Nov 30 for mention pending a probation report from the Welfare Department, as both accused are juveniles.
They were also ordered not to disturb the victim.
Earlier, family members of both accused gathered outside the court building as the duo arrived in a police truck with other detainees about 9am.
They were then escorted by policemen through a side entrance to the lock-up.
993181541249c2c0: SEREMBAN, Oct 16 — The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, conferred the state’s prestigious honours on three Undangs and their consorts at Istana Besar Seri Menanti here yesterday.

The Negeri Sembilan State Secretary’s Office said in a statement today that the three Undangs - Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari of Luak Sungei Ujong, Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi of Luak Jelebu and Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid of Luak Rembau — were conferred the Darjah Tertinggi Negeri Sembilan (DTNS).

Their consorts - Tok Puan Sharifah Amirah Ir Syed Ismail Ash-Shahab of Sungei Ujong, Tok Puan Datin Norazizan Mamat of Jelebu and Tok Puan Asmah Yaakob of Rembau - were honoured with the Darjah Mulia Negeri Sembilan (DMNS).
The statement said the DTNS was reserved for the four Undangs and the Tunku Besar Tampin, while the DMNS was reserved for their consorts.

Also present at the ceremony were the Tunku Ampuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-‘Abidin.
Other attendees included State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim, State Legal Adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal and State Financial Officer Datuk Masri Razali. — Bernama
853e8b9542d90c79: KANGAR: Mahkamah Sesyen memerintahkan pendakwah bebas Ahmad Husam Muhamad Baderudin atau lebih dikenali sebagai Ustaz Husam, membela diri atas pertuduhan menerima gelaran dan kehormatan tidak diiktiraf pada 2023.
Hakim Sharifah Norazlita Syed Salim Idid membuat keputusan itu, selepas mendapati pihak pendakwaan berjaya membuktikan kes prima facie terhadap Husam, 36.
Mahkamah menetapkan 17 dan 18 Dis, untuk prosiding bela diri.
Pada 26 Sept 2024, Husam mengaku tidak bersalah atas pertuduhan itu di hadapan hakim yang sama.
Husam didakwa menerima gelaran dan kehormatan tidak diiktiraf daripada Yang Dipertua Negeri Melaka di Pejabat Jabatan Siasatan Jenayah Komersial, IPK Perlis di sini pada 11.30 pagi, 4 Mei 2023.

Beliau didakwa mengikut Seksyen 4A (3) Enakmen Lambang-Lambang dan Nama-Nama (Mencegah Penggunaan Tidak Betul) (Pindaan) 2016 (Enakmen A21), dibaca bersama Seksyen 17 Akta Kesalahan yang berhubungan dengan Anugerah 2017 (Akta 787) dan boleh dihukum di bawah Seksyen 4A (6) Enakmen Lambang-Lambang dan Nama-Nama (Mencegah Penggunaan Tidak Betul) (Pindaan) 2016 (Enakmen A21).
Jika sabit kesalahan, boleh didenda tidak kurang daripada RM250,000 dan tidak melebihi RM500,000 atau dipenjara selama tempoh tidak kurang daripada satu hingga lima tahun atau kedua-duanya.
Prosiding hari ini dikendalikan Pengarah Pendakwaan Negeri Perlis Mohd Izham Ali, manakala peguam N Sivananthan mewakili Husam.

1bdd633935c498ae: KUCHING: The increase in the interim special grant to Sarawak to RM1.5 billion is not a definitive solution, said Deputy Minister in the Sarawak Premier's Department (Law, MA63 and State-Federal Relations) Datuk Sharifah Hasidah Sayeed Aman Ghazali.
She said the Sarawak government would continue to push for a clear and consistent formula to be established under Article 112D of the Federal Constitution.
"For a long-term solution, the Sarawak government has proposed that a clear and consistent formula be established to determine the rate of the special grant.

"The proposed formula is still being discussed by the Sarawak and Federal governments, and no final formula has been agreed upon so far," she said during the question-and-answer session at the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly sitting here today.
Sharifah Hasidah was responding to a question from Royston Valentine (GPS-Tellian) on the latest status of claims under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) following the interim special grant.

In response to a supplementary question on Sarawak's stance in the event of a change in the Federal administration, she stressed that the state government would continue to champion Sarawak's rights under MA63, regardless of who led the federal government.
On Sept 16, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced an increase in Sarawak's interim special grant to RM1.5 billion from RM600 million, effective this year.
2978c2f8c9e7d501: SEGAMAT: A 70-year-old man suffered a forehead injury after he was struck with a can of glue by a 47-year-old man suspected of sniffing the substance outside a business premises in Jalan Mohd Yusof, Kampung Abdullah, here.
The incident is believed to have occurred after the suspect became angry when the victim told him to stop being noisy outside the premises.
District police chief Superintendent Mohd Jumazanzahir Chek Ismail said preliminary investigations found that the suspect had a criminal record with 33 entries, including for drug-related offences.
"After assaulting the victim, the suspect fled, leaving the victim with a forehead injury. The victim subsequently sought treatment at Segamat Hospital.

"Investigations also found that the suspect was believed to have been involved in a fight at another location before the incident, but no police report was lodged over the altercation," he said in a statement.
Jumazanzahir said, that acting on information received, a team from the district police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Department arrested a man believed to be involved in the incident.
Police also seized a can of glue, a shirt and a pair of jeans to assist in the investigation.
"Upon questioning, the suspect admitted to being involved in the incident," said Jumazanzahir.

He said the case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means, which carries a sentence of a jail term of up to 10 years, with a fine or whipping, or any two of the punishments.
Those with information on the incident are urged to contact the district police headquarters hotline at 07-9324222 or visit the nearest police station to assist investigation.
051a86bc382b9a0e: PETALING JAYA: A marital dispute is believed to have led to the death of Norhazwani Ibrahim, the civil servant allegedly murdered by her husband at the KLIA quarters last night.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Alzafny Ahmad said preliminary investigations found that the 35-year-old Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) officer had been stabbed.

He said Nilai police received a report at 9.30pm that a local man had surrendered at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi police station in Sepang, Selangor, and informed police of his wife’s death at a residence in a public housing complex in Nilai.

"A police team was sent to the location, where they found an unconscious woman in her 30s. A medical team from the Nilai health clinic later confirmed her death," he was quoted as saying by Berita Harian today.

Alzafny said police seized the suspected murder weapon and several other items to assist investigations. The suspect was remanded until Oct 22 for investigation under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
Alzafny said Norhazwani, previously reported to be a customs officer, had been transferred to AKPS effective July 1.

f3e4678a09cdc178: SEREMBAN: The leadership and staff of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) have extended their condolences to the family of a female officer who was allegedly murdered by her husband last night.
MCBA director-general Datuk Seri Shuhaily Mohd Zain and the agency's staff conveyed their condolences to the family of the 35-year-old officer in a post on the agency's Facebook page.
Norhazwani Ibrahim was a Customs Officer Grade WK1 who transferred to the MCBA scheme and was stationed at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
"Her passing is deeply felt by her colleagues and the entire MCBA community. May her service, sacrifices and good deeds throughout her career continue to bring her blessings," the post said.
It was reported that the victim was allegedly murdered by her husband at the KLIA quarters in Jalan Kuarters KLIA, Nilai, last night.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad had said that preliminary investigations showed the victim had been stabbed, with the weapon recovered at the scene.
b0c9cbd363e0606f: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 16 — PKR will contest nine state seats under Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the upcoming Melaka state election on November 14, party secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh said.
She said the names of PKR candidates, together with those from other PH component parties, would be officially announced by coalition chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on October 24.
Fuziah said the announcement would be made during the launch of the PH election machinery at the parking lot of Hang Jebat Stadium in Melaka at 8pm.
“PKR has committed to nine seats as part of PH’s efforts to mount a strong challenge in the Melaka polls.

“The party’s preparations for the state election are now in its final stages, with the candidate selection almost finalised,” she told reporters after the launch of the Southern Zone International Franchise Exhibition tour at the Paradigm Mall Convention Centre here today.
Fuziah was speaking in her capacity as deputy minister of domestic trade and cost of living.
She said PKR’s priority was to ensure all preparations were in place to mount a competitive challenge.
She added that the party would contest only under PH, as no formal political or electoral agreements had been made with other parties.
“Any strategy regarding potential cooperation with other parties are part of PKR’s internal planning.
“However, PKR welcomes any form of support from other parties wishing to assist the coalition for the upcoming Melaka state election,” she said.
In the 2021 state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 of the 28 seats, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional won two.
The Election Commission has set October 31 for nomination, November 10 for early voting and November 14 for polling, following the dissolution of the Melaka state assembly on September 23.
1758c32cfd8015ae: PETALING JAYA: Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) akan menjadikan konvensyen di Kudat, Ahad ini sebagai medan memperkukuh kesiapsiagaan menghadapi PRU16, selain menilai kemajuan agenda pembangunan negeri.

0143ff85cd4bf0f9: PETALING JAYA: The ruling Gabungan Rakyat Sabah will hold its annual convention on Sunday, where delegates are expected to discuss preparations for the next general election (GE16).

GRS secretary-general Armizan Mohd Ali said the convention will take place at Dewan Tun Mustapha in Kudat, in line with the top leadership's decision to hold the annual gathering in different districts each year.

Armizan said the convention will gather central and divisional leaders on one platform for two key reasons - to discuss GRS's political strategy and preparation for GE16, and to evaluate the status of the state government's development efforts.
Grassroots leaders unable to attend the convention may submit their feedback and input online through a platform prepared by the GRS headquarters' secretariat, he said in a statement.
GRS chairman Hajiji Noor will deliver the keynote speech at the convention, while his six deputy chairmen will also address the delegates.
GRS comprises Hajiji's Parti Gagasan Rakyat Sabah, Parti Bersatu Sabah, Upko, Parti Harapan Rakyat Sabah, Parti Cinta Sabah, and the Liberal Democratic Party.
Last week, Armizan said GRS could win more than 15 parliamentary seats based on a simulation of the last state election’s results.
The coalition currently has seven MPs in the Dewan Rakyat.
