bd9b0925b7496e6a: OCTOBER 16 — The High Court on Wednesday (October 14) dismissed former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application to stay the execution of his 15-year prison sentence and RM11.38 billion fine in the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) corruption case.
Justice Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin ruled that Najib failed to establish the special circumstances required to justify a stay pending his ongoing appeals.
The learned judge said that after weighing the arguments from both the prosecution and defence, the gravity of the offences was a more important public interest consideration.
Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak at the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex Oct 14, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif

When asked where the former prime minister was currently serving his sentence, Najib’s lead counsel Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah answered: “He is still in Kajang prison because we have not raised the RM50 million [fine]. Once it is paid, he will be transferred to his house.”

But Najib is already in prison not only because he is serving his sentence in the 1MDB corruption case until his appeal against conviction and sentence is heard, but he is currently serving his sentence stemming from a separate conviction in the SRC International trial.

Now that the Federal Territories Pardons Board has announced that Najib can serve the remainder of his reduced SRC sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to conditions including payment of a RM50 million fine, will he be allowed to serve the house arrest when his sentence in the 1MDB case has not been stayed?
When royal pardon meets court decision, which takes precedence?
Shouldn’t public interest be the overarching consideration?
* This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
f2e85d1199cfc83a: NEW DELHI: Security was stepped up, and police warned of traffic disruptions in the Indian capital, Delhi, on Friday as the 'cockroach' movement called for a rally in the central business district, it's latest in a series of protests demanding the resignation of India's election chief.

The youth-led 'Cockroach Janta Party', opposition groups, and student organisations have held almost daily protests this month demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter lists that critics say favours prime minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party.

More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision, but the Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke called Friday's flag protest in support of two CJP leaders detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at a protest site in violation of a ban.
CJP and left-wing student groups have urged supporters to gather at Central Park in New Delhi's busy Connaught Place shopping and food district on Friday evening to wave and hoist the national flag.

Delhi Police, however, urged people not to join "such assemblies", and the civic authority announced late on Thursday that the park itself would be closed for two days "due to administrative reasons".
Police said they can facilitate a group of select people to carry the national flag and sing the national anthem at a "suitable place".

Traders in the area petitioned the Supreme Court to prevent the protest, which they say "would cause severe loss", and demanded compensation for losses suffered during a similar rally planned over the weekend that was foiled by a security crackdown.
The cockroach movement has emerged as one of the biggest political challenges faced by Modi and his BJP in his 12 years in power.
A weeks-long sit-in by its supporters earlier this year forced education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over exam paper leaks.

The latest demonstrations erupted after The Indian Express newspaper reported that Kumar's two deputies raised concerns internally about voter list changes, registration procedures and digital systems.
438cab28e903b54a: KUALA LUMPUR: A comprehensive assessment will be conducted before any decision is made on appointing a new head coach for Harimau Malaya, amid speculation linking Japanese coach Hajime Moriyasu to the role.
Youth and Sports Minister Dr Taufiq Johari said discussions would be held with the FA of Malaysia (FAM) and key stakeholders to ensure the appointment yields the best outcomes for national football.
A top-level Japanese coach could demand a salary of up to US$60,000 (about RM252,000) a month.

"It is still under discussion. We will hold discussions with FAM and all the stakeholders involved because the most important thing is to ensure that it delivers the best possible returns for the country.
"We will carry out an overall assessment based on performance, work processes and so on, before making a decision and announcing it," he said yesterday.
Moriyasu has been linked with the post as Malaysia seek to secure qualification for the 2030 FIFA World Cup.
FAM reportedly has not ruled out hiring a foreign coach following the formation of a new executive committee to strengthen the squad for the 2030 World Cup qualifying campaign.
However, the governing body is also open to retaining a local coach if the candidate can deliver results.
FAM president Datuk Ab Ghani Hassan said the final decision would not rest with him alone, but would be decided by the executive committee.
Harimau Malaya are currently under interim coach Tan Cheng Hoe, who led the team to a third-place finish in the Asean Cup.
During the group stage, Malaysia defeated Bangladesh 6-0, drew 0-0 with Indonesia, and beat Singapore 6-0 to finish second and miss out on the final.
Cheng Hoe's side then edged Vietnam 1-0 in the third-place playoff.
44399f4ebdc8d2ba: PETALING JAYA: PKR sah akan bertanding sembilan kerusi pada PRN Melaka bulan depan, kata Setiausaha Agungnya, Fuziah Salleh.
"Calon kita lebih kurang sudah dimuktamadkan, insya-Allah. Setakat ini, kita akan bertanding di sembilan kerusi dan Pakatan Harapan (PH) tentunya akan bertanding lebih banyak kerusi.

"Perkara paling penting bagi kita di Melaka adalah memastikan persiapan sudah dilakukan dan kita akan memberikan saingan yang sangat baik, insya-Allah," katanya menurut Berita Harian selepas Majlis Perasmian Jelajah Pameran Francais Antarabangsa Zon Selatan di Johor Bahru.

Beliau berkata, senarai calon PKR akan diumumkan Presidennya, Anwar Ibrahim, yang juga pengerusi PH dalam Majlis Pengumuman Calon dan Pelancaran Jentera PH PRN Melaka di tapak parkir Stadium Hang Jebat, Melaka, pada 8 malam 24 Okt ini.
Fuziah berkata, tiada persefahaman rasmi dimeterai dengan mana-mana parti setakat ini, tetapi PKR mengalu-alukan sebarang bentuk bantuan daripada pihak lain yang mahu membantunya pada PRN Melaka.
"Kalau ada pihak yang mahu membantu, kita amat mengalu-alukan."
Hari penamaan calon PRN Melaka ditetapkan pada 31 Okt ini dan hari mengundi pada 14 Nov nanti.
Dewan Undangan Negeri Melaka mempunyai 28 kerusi, dengan Barisan Nasional memenangi 21 kerusi, PH (5) dan Perikatan Nasional (2) pada PRN lalu.
f48aaf4121a4867e: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — The Road Transport (Amendment) Act 2026, which amends the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333), came into force today, introducing new provisions to curb illegal street racing and ‘tonto’ syndicate activities, as well as strengthen enforcement and the digitalisation of Road Transport Department (JPJ) services.
The Transport Ministry (MOT) said the Act, which contains 42 amendment clauses, was part of the government’s efforts to improve road safety, strengthen enforcement and modernise JPJ service delivery.
According to the ministry, one of the key changes is the introduction of Section 42A, which makes racing or testing speed on public roads a specific offence.
“This provision enables enforcement action to be taken without having to wait for an accident, injury or loss of life to occur,” MOT said in a statement today.
For a first conviction, offenders may be fined between RM2,000 and RM10,000, or jailed for up to two years, or both.
For a second or subsequent conviction, offenders may be fined between RM5,000 and RM20,000, or jailed for up to five years, or both.

MOT said the Act also introduces Section 110B to address ‘tonto’ syndicate activities that obstruct or interfere with enforcement operations, including tailing enforcement vehicles and relaying information about operations.
“Those convicted of the offence may be fined between RM10,000 and RM50,000, or jailed for between one and five years, or both. The offence is also categorised as an arrestable offence,” it said.
The ministry said other amendments strengthen the accountability of registered vehicle owners for offences detected by enforcement cameras, including automated enforcement systems.
“These amendments aim to close legal loopholes that could allow certain parties to evade responsibility for offences committed using their vehicles,” the ministry said.

MOT said the amendments also strengthen the legal basis for the use of electronic licences, documents, records and notices, while paving the way for digital accident reporting in accordance with prescribed procedures.
In addition, regulations governing the safety of electric vehicles, modified vehicles, vehicle components and micromobility vehicles have been strengthened.

“MOT believes that the implementation of the amendments to Act 333 will strengthen enforcement agencies’ ability to curb activities that endanger road safety, while making public services more convenient through the use of technology and digital services,” it said.

The ministry further said the increase in the maximum compound limit for compoundable offences from RM300 to RM500 would take effect on Jan 1, 2029, to allow sufficient transition time for road users.

“MOT wishes to clarify that the increase in the maximum compound limit does not mean that all traffic offences will automatically incur a RM500 compound. The amount offered is subject to the type of offence and the rules prescribed under Act 333.
“The measure aims to improve legal compliance and provide a more effective deterrent, rather than burdening the public or increasing government revenue,” the ministry stressed. — Bernama
cb5d070eb9cbc6aa: JOHOR BARU: An Indonesian food producer has secured an export deal worth about RM550,000 to supply seasoning products to Malaysia, as a separate cross-border partnership explores potential investment and business opportunities worth another RM408,000.
The two agreements, facilitated by the Indonesian Consulate-General in Johor Baru at Trade Expo Indonesia (TEI) 2026 in Tangerang today, have a combined indicative value of nearly RM960,000.

The food supply contract, worth US$134,652 (about RM550,000), was signed between Indonesia's CV Berkah Pangan Nusantara, based in Sidoarjo, East Java, and Malaysian trading company MAW Global Trading.
The agreement covers exports of seasoned flour, cooking spices and condiments for distribution in Johor and Pahang.
MAW Global Trading representative Ahmad Amirul Latepi, said demand for Indonesian processed food products remained a promising market opportunity in southern Peninsular Malaysia and the east coast.
CV Berkah Pangan Nusantara director Ryza Sulistyanawati said the company was ready to maintain a consistent supply of quality products to meet Malaysian demand and expand its distribution network.

The second agreement, valued indicatively at US$100,000 (about RM408,000), brings together the Dumai chapter of the Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KADIN) and the Malay Economic Development Chamber (MEDC).
The proposed collaboration covers oil and gas, integrated business development, skills certification for skilled workers, tourism and health tourism.
MEDC president Zaini Atan said the agreement provided a starting point for developing concrete cross-border business partnerships.
He added there is a need to strengthen Indonesian workers' technical and vocational education and training (TVET) to meet modern Malaysian industry standards.
While KADIN Dumai chairman Zulfan Ismaini said the parties would follow up with technical business meetings involving companies from Dumai and Malaysia.
Indonesian Consul-General in Johor Baru Sigit S. Widiyanto, who witnessed both signings, said follow-up action would be critical to translating the agreements into tangible economic benefits.

He said the food export deal could open opportunities to expand distribution into Melaka and Negri Sembilan, while the KADIN-MEDC partnership could lead to new investment opportunities across priority sectors.
6828de0d8b534aaa: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must invest in dedicated sports science support for their athletes to challenge for medals at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, a sports specialist said.

Sports science specialist Dr Ahmad Fazli Ahmad Idris said athletes preparing for the Olympics needed direct access to specialists in sports psychology, recovery and nutrition, rather than treating these areas as secondary to daily training.
"Stop treating sports science as an afterthought," he told sports reporter K. Rajan on the Timesport: On The Beat podcast.

Fazli called on the National Sports Council (NSC) and National Sports Institute (NSI) to assign dedicated personnel to athletes who qualify for LA 2028, with at least a sports psychologist and massage therapist included in their support teams.
"Daily training takes a heavy toll, and proper recovery and nutrition are vital. Invest in these athletes for the next two years," he said.
His call comes after Malaysia matched their best-ever Asian Games gold-medal haul with nine golds at the recent Aichi-Nagoya Games, equalling the 2010 tally in Guangzhou.
Although the contingent surpassed their initial target of six golds, Fazli said Malaysia must do more to close the gap on Asian sporting powerhouses China, Japan and South Korea.
"For me, we did well, but not well enough," he said.
He said Malaysia's preparations for LA 2028 must form part of a long-term development plan, rather than a short-term push centred on established stars and immediate results.
Fazli said national sports associations should work towards an eight-year development cycle to build a bigger pool of competitive athletes and reduce reliance on individuals.
"Relying on just one person is our core problem; the entire support system is what matters," he said.
He added that athletes needed proper education and financial security so they could focus on training without worrying about their future careers.
He warned that without a structured development programme and consistent support, Malaysia risked repeating past mistakes ahead of LA 2028 instead of building on their Asian Games achievement.
"Athletes need to have a future beyond sports. They need proper education and financial support so they can concentrate on their training.
"If we do not have a proper system in place, we will keep repeating the same mistakes. We need to build on what we have achieved and prepare properly for LA 2028."
* Timesport: On the Beat is available on YouTube, Spotify, Audioplus and Apple Podcasts
da8b8e983a31ffd0: SHANGHAI: China stocks rebounded on Friday from the previous session’s 14-month lows, after a slew of AI-related companies proposed share buybacks or forecast stellar growth, but the market is still on track for its worst week in three months.
Sentiment was also aided by a rebound in global equities following Thursday’s savage selling in AI stocks triggered by concerns over big spending on AI infrastructure as borrowing costs rise.
Stocks in South Korea and Japan bounced after an overnight rebound on Wall Street.
Jitters also eased in China, where the blue-chip CSI300 Index was up 0.8% by the lunch break, while the Shanghai Composite Index rose 1%.
Still, the CSI300 Index is poised to drop roughly 3% for the week, the worst showing since July. The gauge is also set to record a 10-week losing streak.

Tech shares recouped some of their recent losses after at least 10 AI supply chain companies, including optical transceiver maker Eoptolink and chip equipment maker Piotech, announced share buyback or stock purchase plans.
In addition, a string of tech companies including chipmakers MetaX Integrated Circuits and Hygon Information Technology published third-quarter profit forecasts that signal torrid growth.

*Sentiment remains subdued amid global liquidity headwinds," Morgan Stanley said in a China equity strategy report on Friday. "Weak domestic demand and less-supportive liquidity and flows continue to limit index upside."

At a meeting in Bangkok on Friday, US Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh said he was optimistic about the impact of AI and believed it would change the real economy, but its near-term impact on employment was uncertain.
Warsh also said the Fed needed to think about financial stability risks, as traders closely monitor the US monetary policy path.
Real estate, gold and defense stocks led the gains in China on Friday, rising more than 3%.
In Hong Kong, biotech and property shares jumped.
1616c604f484333a: PETALING JAYA: The Sarawak government is temporarily using alternative methods to deliver healthcare to the state’s interior following the suspension of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) after a fatal helicopter crash at Long Lellang, Baram, on Sept 8.

Sarawak deputy public health, housing and local government minister Michael Tiang said mobile clinic teams were being deployed using four-wheel-drive vehicles and boats to reach accessible areas, while the government worked on a proposal to improve the FDS’s safety and effectiveness.

Tiang said the government was also coordinating emergency medical evacuations using other air assets, including the fire and rescue department’s air unit, the police air wing, and the Royal Malaysian Air Force.

“The government will continue to evaluate and improve its healthcare delivery methods to ensure rural communities have access to the necessary services,” Borneo Post quoted him as saying in the state assembly today.

He said the proposal would outline comprehensive improvements to the FDS, including operational safety, emergency training and preparedness, personnel welfare and protection, and aircraft suitability and capability.

In the Sept 8 incident, a Bolkow BO-105 helicopter operated by Layang Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd under a health ministry contract crashed at the Long Lellang airstrip in Ulu Baram, killing the pilot and four medical workers.

Transport minister Loke Siew Fook said in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday an initial investigation report would be presented to the Cabinet today and a final report completed within a year of the accident.
63d3ff7147390989: KOTA KINABALU: The Zara Qairina Mahathir tragedy has affected not just the teen's family, but many others.
These included the five minors who were accused of verbal abuse and bullying of the 13-year-old prior to her death, said Joan Goh, the lawyer for one of the girls.

In a statement after the conclusion of the inquest into Zara Qairina's death, where Amir Shah Amir Hassan, acting as coroner, set Jan 15 to deliver his verdict, she asked the public to refrain from drawing conclusions and making unwarranted accusations.
She said the public should allow the judicial process to take its proper course without resorting to sensationalism or speculation.
She said the tragedy had affected not only Zara Qairina's family but also the children caught in the midst of intense public scrutiny.
Zara Qairina died on July 17 last year, a day after she was found lying unconscious on the ground floor of SMKA Tun Datu Mustapha hostel.
"Our thoughts remain with the family of Zara. After all this is still a tragic loss to the family.
"However, the pursuit of justice for Zara must never come at the expense of justice for others.

"Whilst we fully respect the public's concern and desire for justice, it is equally important to remember that these are children whose rights, welfare and future must also be protected," Goh said in a statement.
Speaking to reporters, Goh's colleague Prem Elmer Ganasan said the 96-day inquest must be fair to reflect all evidence adduced by the individuals and respective experts in the field.
He said among them were forensic pathologist psychiatrists, investigating officer among others.

"We would like to thank all parties involved through these 96 days of inquest into the death of the late Zara," he said, adding that he was delivering the message on behalf of his team leader Datuk Ram Singh.

The team of conducting officers comprises former Sabah prosecution director and now Melaka prosecution director Nahra Dollah as well as deputy public prosecutors Mohd Fairuz Johari, Dana Arabi Wazani, Sofia S Sawayan, and Dacia Jane Romanus.

Zara Qairina's mother Noraidah Lamat was represented by Shahlan Jufri, Datuk Rizwandean Bukhary M. Borhan, Mohd Luqman Syazwan Zabidi Md Zain, Mohd Syarulnizam Mohd Salleh, Farrah Nasser and Elhanan James.
The girl's father Mahathir Mohd Hashim, meanwhile, was represented by Sherzali Herza Asli, Nurul Rafeeqa Afdul Mutolip, and Clarice Vyone Conrad.
Azhier Farhan Arisin, Abdul Fikry Jaafar Abdullah, Mohammed Fareez Mohammed Salleh, and Sylyester Kuan acted for Students B, C, D and E.
16bf6f434eb9070a: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — All school bus owners and operators have been urged to update their drivers’ details from today until October 30 to facilitate the disbursement of RM1,000 in special financial assistance.
The Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) said in a statement today that the information could be updated through its official portal at https://bantuanpemandu.mot.gov.my/bas-sekolah.
The required information includes each driver’s current name, address, telephone number, valid driving and Public Service Vehicle (PSV) licences, and bank account number for payment.

APAD said the exercise was aimed at ensuring eligible school bus drivers receive the assistance as soon as possible, in line with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s call for payments to be completed before Deepavali.

The agency said it had also engaged with the Federation of Malaysian School Bus Associations and the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor School Bus Operators Association to ensure an orderly and accurate eligibility verification and payment process.
As part of the process, drivers’ records will be cross-checked against databases maintained by APAD, the Commercial Vehicle Licensing Board (LPKP) and the Road Transport Department (JPJ).
This includes checking the validity of driving and PSV licences to ensure recipients meet the eligibility requirements.
Payments will be made in phases starting Oct 22.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke previously said about 53,000 taxi, hire car and school bus drivers were expected to receive a one-off payment of RM1,000 each before Deepavali. — Bernama
8d2ca3855c132cc6: PETALING JAYA: Two sisters died after being trapped in a fire that destroyed two adjoining houses at Kampung Koh in Sitiawan, Perak, today.

Perak fire and rescue department director Sayani Saidon said his team received information about the incident at 9am. Personnel from the Sitiawan and Seri Manjung fire stations were deployed to the scene.
"Two girls aged 18 and 15 were trapped in their home. Both were confirmed dead," he was reported as saying by Utusan Malaysia.
The two-storey, semi-detached houses measuring 40ft by 70ft each were mostly destroyed by the blaze.
Saidon said the fire also damaged four vehicles: two Proton Sagas, a Proton Perdana and a motorcycle.
He said the fire was contained at 10.30am and checks were made to eliminate any remaining embers or other flammable materials that could reignite the blaze.
A total of 20 personnel, including members of the Pantai Remis volunteer fire brigade, took part in the operation, while the K9 unit assisted with the investigation.
8dcc8ebefc28a640: PETALING JAYA: Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd digesa menambah genset bergerak di tiga sekolah menengah berasrama di Tongod susulan kerosakan dua transformer utama yang menjejaskan bekalan elektrik di daerah itu sejak minggu lalu.

Adun Kuamut Masiung Banah berkata bekalan sementara perlu disalurkan segera ke Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Tongod, SMK Penangah dan SMK Entilibon kerana asrama di sekolah berkenaan bergelap pada waktu malam.

Katanya, keadaan itu menyebabkan pelajar terpaksa menggunakan cahaya lilin untuk belajar dan mengulang kaji pelajaran, termasuk mereka yang bakal menduduki peperiksaan Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) dan Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM).
“Saya menerima aduan daripada guru dan ibu bapa bahawa pelajar terpaksa mengulang kaji menggunakan cahaya lilin di asrama dan rumah sejak minggu lalu kerana ketiadaan bekalan elektrik.
“Saya menggesa Sabah Electricity menambah genset bergerak di tiga sekolah terbabit bagi membantu calon SPM dan STPM belajar dan membuat persediaan menghadapi peperiksaan,” katanya dalam kenyataan.

Masiung berkata empat genset bergerak berkapasiti keseluruhan 2,000kW sudah ditempatkan sebagai sokongan sementara di Tongod, namun bekalan itu masih tidak mencukupi sehingga menjejaskan operasi tiga sekolah berkenaan.
Menurutnya, beliau dimaklumkan pejabat Sabah Electricity di Telupid bahawa transformer yang membekalkan tenaga elektrik ke Tongod mengalami kerosakan sejak minggu lalu.

Beliau berkata sudah menghubungi pejabat Sabah Electricity di Telupid bagi mendapatkan penjelasan dan berharap genset tambahan dapat dihantar ke tiga sekolah itu sementara kerja membaiki transformer utama dijalankan.

Sementara itu, Pegawai Pembangunan Masyarakat (PPM) Tokyo Hasim Omar berkata gangguan bekalan elektrik sering berlaku di Tongod sejak bulan lalu sehingga menjejaskan urusan pentadbiran beberapa jabatan kerajaan.
Beliau berkata kapasiti transformer sedia ada mungkin tidak lagi mampu menampung permintaan semasa berikutan peningkatan jumlah pengguna dari tahun ke tahun.
Tokyo turut menggesa Sabah Electricity menggantikan transformer sedia ada dengan unit berkapasiti lebih besar bagi menampung pertambahan bangunan kerajaan dan kediaman di daerah itu.
c54ad62722cf0d22: IPOH: Years of hard work developing fruit orchards in Bukit Bangkong, Chemor, are under threat after wild elephants raided the area three times within weeks, damaging fruit trees, water tanks, pipes and ponds.
The elephants were first spotted on Sept 27 before returning on Oct 3 and Oct 11, damaging fruit trees, water tanks, pipes and ponds.

Abdul Rahim Ahmad, 65, who represents the Bukit Bangkong Hulu Cemor farmers' group, said the repeated incursions had raised concerns among orchard owners who had invested considerable time, effort and money in developing their land.
"We have worked hard to develop these orchards and we are also contributing to the country's food security.
"If the elephants keep returning, our crops and property could be destroyed. We are worried they may come back for a fourth or fifth time," he said.
Abdul Rahim said the damage included broken branches on jackfruit, coconut and durian trees, as well as damaged water tanks and pipes used to supply water to the orchards.
He said more than 40 coconut trees in his orchard alone had been affected, while neighbouring farmers had also suffered damage to their fruit trees and other property.
The elephants had also entered several ponds, apparently to wallow in the water, adding to the cost of repairs.
Abdul Rahim said hiring an excavator cost about RM1,000 a day, while rebuilding a pond could take two to three days.
He said he had lodged a police report after the first incident on Sept 27 for referral to the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan).

Following the second incident, the farmers contacted Perhilitan again, prompting officers to visit the area the next day to monitor the situation and advise them on safety measures and possible compensation.
However, he urged the authorities to take further action, including driving the elephants away or relocating them to prevent further damage.
"We have invested a lot of time, energy and money in developing these fruit orchards. We are also contributing to food security by producing food.
"We hope the authorities will help us find a solution before the situation gets worse," he said.
Abdul Rahim said the total losses had yet to be assessed, as the extent of the damage varied among orchard owners.
Meanwhile, another orchard owner, Omar Abdullah, 70, said the repeated incursions had affected not only the farmers' livelihoods but also their morale.
"Every orchard the elephants enter suffers some form of damage. In my orchard, the affected items include durian, jackfruit and coconut trees, water tanks and water pipes.
"More importantly, our morale has been affected. We need support from the relevant authorities to restore our confidence and enable us to continue farming," he said.
The retired teacher said about 12 orchard lots belonging to 12 owners had been affected.
He said the land had been allocated by the government for cultivation, with seedlings supplied by the Agriculture Department, and that the farmers had worked hard to develop their orchards.

He urged the authorities to address the problem effectively, warning that failure to protect the farmers' efforts could undermine their livelihoods and the government's efforts to strengthen agricultural production.
Perak Perhilitan director Dr Pazil Abdul Patah confirmed today that the department had received complaints about the matter.
"We have received complaints and conducted monitoring in the area. We will try to capture the elephants," he said.

07036406c3dff99e: KUCHING, Oct 16 — The increase in the interim payment of the special grant to Sarawak to RM1.5 billion does not constitute a definitive solution, said Deputy Minister in the Sarawak Premier’s Department (Law, MA63 and State-Federal Relations) Datuk Sharifah Hasidah Sayeed Aman Ghazali.
She stressed that the Sarawak government would continue to push for a clear and consistent formula to be established under Article 112D of the Federal Constitution.
“For a long-term solution, the Sarawak government has proposed that a clear and consistent formula be established to determine the rate of the special grant.

“The proposed formula is still being discussed by the Sarawak and Federal governments, and no final formula has been agreed upon so far,” she said during the question-and-answer session at the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly sitting here today.
Sharifah Hasidah was responding to a question from Royston Valentine (GPS-Tellian) on the latest status of claims under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) following the interim special grant.

In response to a supplementary question on Sarawak’s stance in the event of a change in the Federal administration, she stressed that the state government would continue to champion Sarawak’s rights under MA63, regardless of who led the Federal government.
On September 16, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced an increase in Sarawak’s interim special grant to RM1.5 billion, up from RM600 million previously, effective this year. — Bernama
e6df94983e89f882: JAKARTA, Oct 16 — Four people died on Indonesia’s Java island fighting the blazes that have been sending toxic smoke across southeast Asia, closing schools and fuelling a surge of respiratory complaints in the region, authorities said today.
The impact of the months-long fires has prompted Singapore’s leader to vow legal action against any companies responsible for the blazes that have made regional air quality among the world’s worst.
Singapore again topped IQAir’s live ranking of the world’s most polluted major cities today, with Kuala Lumpur second and Jakarta sixth.

“Where warranted, we will take action under Singapore’s Transboundary Haze Pollution Act, and also explore joint action with other countries,” said Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, without giving further details.
Singapore has no plantations or forests of its own, but several companies with concessions in Indonesia are reportedly based in the city-state.
Legal experts have cautioned that pursuing companies linked to the smoke is challenging, with investigations reliant on cooperation from foreign authorities.
Singapore enacted the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act in 2014, after a severe pollution episode in 2013. Another spell occurred in 2015.
The law allows authorities to target companies whose activities overseas cause or contribute to unhealthy haze levels in Singapore.
Establishing responsibility is challenging because it requires authorities to share maps pinpointing fire hotspots, with overlapping land claims further complicating matters.
Singapore’s investigations into four Indonesian companies over their alleged role in the 2015 haze crisis remain open, a case that strained relations with Jakarta at the time.
Other chances for legal action, including a possible case at The Hague-based International Court of Justice, were also low as it needed Indonesia’s consent for jurisdiction in the case.
‘Do everything we can’
Singapore’s air pollution surged to 251 on IQAir’s Air Quality Index level into very unhealthy levels at around 0400 GMT today.
Under the Swiss-based company’s system, readings of 151-200 are considered unhealthy, 201-300 very unhealthy and above 300 hazardous.
“We cannot control the weather or the winds, nor can we directly control what happens beyond our borders,” said Wong.
“But we will do everything we can to protect Singaporeans, while working with our neighbours to address the underlying causes of the haze.”

The smoke is a direct consequence of the fires, which four people lost their lives battling in East Java’s Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park yesterday, Indonesia’s forestry ministry said in a statement.
Two others suffered serious burns and are receiving further medical treatment.
“This incident serves as a reminder that forest and land fire extinguishing is a high-risk operation,” it said, adding personnel safety remained a primary concern.
The forestry department in the same statement said there was a significant jump in hotspots in several areas in six “priority provinces” where 615 so-called hotspots were detected.
A hotspot is a location where a satellite detects an unusually high temperature, indicating a potential fire or other strong heat source. — AFP
1d448085f6b84d02: KOTA BARU: Pas and Umno are expected to finalise seat allocations for the Melaka election within the next two days, with discussions focusing on the remaining seats.

He said Pas respected Umno's position in the state and would focus on contesting seats that Umno did not contest.

Amar said BN's allocation of 21 seats in Melaka would remain unchanged, although seat swaps could still be considered in the final stage of negotiations.
He said Umno had indicated its willingness to hold further discussions on possible seat exchanges.
Amar said Pas was not concerned about the arrangement, as Melaka, like Johor, was traditionally an Umno stronghold.
He said Pas was optimistic about its chances in the seven seats it was eyeing, with the party expecting to win at least four.
He added that a special committee was discussing the remaining allocations, with negotiations now focused on finalising the seats.
"At this stage, the committee members are only finalising the seats," he said.

91c70c6b50a0604b: KUALA LUMPUR: Strong order replenishment and growing original design manufacturer (ODM) contributions are expected to underpin Cnergenz Bhd's revenue visibility, with earnings growth expected to strengthen from the second half of financial year 2026 (2H26).
RHB Research said it remained positive on Cnergenz's earnings trajectory as the group entered a stronger growth phase.

This is driven by robust order momentum in its core surface mount technology (SMT) segment amid accelerating artificial intelligence-related capital expenditure, alongside the ramp-up of its ODM AI tester business.
"Management expects financial year 2026 (FY26) to be a record sales year, with growth momentum sustaining into FY27," it said.
The firm maintained its "Buy" call on Cnergenz, while raising its target price to RM1.40 from RM0.92 previously.

According to RHB Research, the ODM products accounted for about 10 per cent of Cnergenz's RM240 million order book, with production ramping up to four units a week from two previously, supported by double-shift operations.
The group is using additional floor space to accommodate near-term production before its new manufacturing facility becomes operational.
The company expects about 57 units to be delivered in FY26, with volumes potentially exceeding 100 units in FY27 as capacity expands.
Further upside could come from additional customer wins by its major equipment maker client, which would accelerate the commercial scaling of Cnergenz's AI tester business.

RHB Research said Cnergenz was planning a new manufacturing facility at Science Park in Batu Kawan to support assembly, automation and ODM AI tester manufacturing, partly funded by about RM32 million in initial public offering proceeds.
Operations at the new facility are targeted to begin by FY28, while the existing Xlent facility will be used for new product introduction and other ad hoc projects.

The firm said the contribution of high-margin Integrated Solutions, which accounted for about 40 per cent of the order book, coupled with operating leverage, could support a recovery in core margins towards historical levels of 10 to 13 per cent recorded between FY18 and FY22.

RHB Research raised its FY26 to FY28 earnings forecasts by 56 per cent, 51 per cent and 52 per cent respectively, reflecting stronger revenue and margin assumptions following robust order book growth.
Order book replenishment of more than 80 per cent within FY26 and planned capacity expansion in FY27 further underpin its growth outlook.
The firm maintained its valuation of 23 times FY27 forecast earnings, deriving a revised target price of RM1.40, inclusive of a two per cent environmental, social and governance discount.
Key risks to its outlook include the timing of order recognition, project execution and foreign exchange exposure.
c3e6cf86a9bf59e3: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Malaysian game studio Metronomik was the big winner at this year’s Level Up SEA Game Awards, sweeping three categories — including the coveted Grand Jury Award — as the annual celebration of South-east Asia’s gaming talent returned for its ninth edition.

Metronomik took home the night’s top honour for Ondeh Ondeh Kaya’s Tasty Tale, which also earned the studio Best Score and Music and Best Technology at the ceremony held yesterday at the Connexion Conference & Event Centre (CCEC).
Malaysia claimed five of the 11 awards presented, with OPNeon Games winning Best Game Design for TCG Card Shop Simulator, while Asia Pacific University picked up Best Student Game for Fish Can Man.

Organised by the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) in conjunction with Level Up KL, South-east Asia’s premier annual game developers conference, the awards celebrate the best independent games from the region and selected international markets.
This year’s edition attracted 174 submissions, including 71 from Malaysia, 34 from Indonesia and 12 from Singapore, according to MDEC chairman Ganesh Kumar Bangah.
Thailand and Vietnam contributed eight entries each, followed by the Philippines with five and Brunei with two. Another 34 submissions came from outside South-east Asia.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Malaysian game studio Metronomik emerged as the night’s biggest winner, scooping three awards for ‘Ondeh Ondeh Kaya’s Tasty Tale’, including the prestigious Grand Jury Award. — Picture courtesy of The Magic Rain

Beyond Malaysia, Indonesian developers also made their mark, with HOOP Studios, a student game studio from Telkom University, winning Best Audio for Mission Mancala, while Authentic Remixes claimed Best Visual Art for Kidbash: Super Legend.
Singapore-based Team Project Lunch picked up Best Storytelling for Compensation Guaranteed: Build A Livable Future Together, while Japan’s PLAYISM secured Best International Game for Homura Hime.
Indonesia’s Bumi Studios won the Audience Choice Award for Little Tree Kingdom, while fellow Indonesian developer InnerSight Games received the Rising Star Award for Voodoo Craft.

Speaking at the ceremony, which brought together game developers, industry figures, enthusiasts and members of the media, Ganesh said the awards were designed to give South-east Asia’s gaming talent greater visibility and opportunities beyond the region.

“The SEA Game Awards was created to celebrate the region’s developers, especially independent studios, and provide a platform where outstanding work can be recognised by peers, partners, publishers and audiences,” he said.
“It is not just a celebration but also a bridge between creative ambition and commercial opportunity.”

Ganesh added that the submissions reflected the diversity of ideas emerging across the region, from small teams developing their first playable games to established studios looking to reach wider international audiences.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Japan’s PLAYISM took home the Best International Game award for ‘Homura Hime’. — Picture courtesy of The Magic Rain

Beyond the trophies, the ceremony also offered a glimpse of what’s coming next, with exclusive game reveals, performances and trailers showcasing upcoming titles from developers across South-east Asia.

Malaysian games featured in the showcase included Project XII by Albrite Studios, TCG Card Shop Simulator by OPNeon Games, Ondeh Ondeh Kaya’s Tasty Tale by Metronomik, Bloodwell by Ten Ten Studio, Overhours by CtrlD Studio and Wira by RICRYM.

Other titles showcased included Fallen Tear: The Ascension by the Philippines’ Winter Crew Studios, Sepak U: Sports Fighting Game by Good Knight Collective, HellHeart Breaker by Singapore’s BattleBrew Productions and Nightmare Circus by Thailand’s Fairplay Studios.
Also featured were Lost & Found Co. by Bit Egg Inc, Dungeon Hot Pot by Indonesia’s Renala Games and 13Z: The Zodiac Trials by Singapore’s Mixed Realms.
Level Up KL and the SEA Game Awards have been part of MDEC’s efforts to grow Malaysia’s game development industry since 2015 and 2017, respectively.

Over the years, both platforms have brought together developers, publishers, investors, technology providers, academics and other industry players through game showcases, business-matching sessions, masterclasses and knowledge-sharing programmes.
Malaysia’s gaming industry has also grown significantly, with the number of game development studios rising from just 30 in 2014 to 112 in 2025, including nine multinational studios.
5e5fd84b14d8e431: KUANTAN: A restaurant manager and an assistant claimed trial in the Sessions Court here today to nine counts of criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving RM58,400.30.
Siti Norsuzuanie Ali, 29, and Muhammad Zulhilmi Ahyauddin, 24, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out to them before judge Sazlina Safie.
The duo were jointly charged with misappropriating money for their own use without the company's authorisation by manipulating refund transactions involving 1,199 receipts in the restaurant's system.
The nine charges involved transactions totalling RM58,400.30, allegedly committed at a restaurant in Pekan between January and September this year, between 9am and 10pm.
The charges were framed under Section 408 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of between one and 14 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.

Deputy public prosecutor Azizah Ahmad proposed bail of RM30,000 for each accused, with additional conditions that they surrender their passports, refrain from interfering with witnesses and report to the nearest police station once a month.
Lawyer Datuk Zaharman Zainal Abidin, representing both accused, sought a lower bail amount.
Sazlina set bail at RM9,000 for each accused, subject to the additional conditions, and fixed Nov 23 for mention.
711fa8bec954f0f8: MUMBAI: India's Reliance Industries rejected Friday suggestions that it was blocking Elon Musk's Starlink satellite internet service in the country, saying it welcomed competition and had "never feared" rivals.

The statement came days after the tech billionaire accused "oligarchs" of preventing Starlink's rollout in India to protect their monopolies, reigniting a long-running debate over access to the country's lucrative telecommunications market.
"We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best," Reliance said in a statement. "We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink."
The conglomerate, owned by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, said it was responding to recent remarks about Reliance and the Indian market but did not directly name Musk.

The potential launch of Starlink, which provides high-speed internet access to remote locations by low Earth orbit satellites, has seen fierce debate in India over issues ranging from pricing to spectrum allocation.
In March 2025, telecom operator Jio Platforms, Reliance's digital arm, signed an agreement with Musk's SpaceX to offer Starlink services to its customers.
However, Starlink has yet to launch, with Jio's own satellite service still awaiting regulatory clearance.
Earlier this month, Musk wrote on X that Starlink was being "blocked" in India.
"Unfortunately, we are being blocked by certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people," Musk said.
"You can guess who they are... This is a crime against the people of India!"
In a subsequent post, Musk addressed Ambani directly, calling him "prime minister" in an apparent jibe at his perceived closeness with prime minister Narendra Modi.
Soon after, India's communications ministry, without mentioning Musk, said the government maintained a "fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework" for all telecom services.
Reliance said on Friday that every operator, including Jio, "must serve the people of India and abide by the laws and policies of the land".
The dispute comes as Reliance pushes deeper into telecommunications and digital services, key pillars of Ambani's drive to diversify the conglomerate beyond its oil refining and petrochemicals roots.

The comments also follow Jio's announcement this week that it plans to raise US$3.2 billion in what would be India's largest initial public offering, after unveiling pricing details ahead of next week's share sale.
d95feaa4e4543c87: SEREMBAN: Punca seorang wanita maut dipercayai ditikam suaminya di Kuarters Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Kuala Lumpur (KLIA) malam tadi ialah akibat perselisihan rumah tangga.

9c54ad116347dfad: KUALA LUMPUR: Much of the work that keeps people connected rarely makes the headlines.

For Ir. Geetha Remy Vincent, MEASAT's Principal of Spectrum & Regulatory Affairs, ensuring that the spectrum resources, policies and industry partnerships needed for future growth are in place is central to Malaysia's digital future.
Her leadership and contributions recently earned her the Women in Tech Leadership (Regulatory and Public Affairs) award at the PIKOM Digital Excellence Awards 2026.
For Geetha, the recognition highlights an often-overlooked area of the technology sector — spectrum management and regulatory leadership.
"Spectrum management and regulatory work may happen behind the scenes, but they are fundamental to keeping communities connected," she said.

She sees the award not only as a personal milestone, but also as recognition of the role that regulation and spectrum management play in supporting connectivity, innovation and digital transformation.
The recognition is also significant for MEASAT as it marks 30 years of pioneering satellite connectivity and supporting the nation's connectivity journey.
Geetha said the milestone reinforced the company's commitment to helping bridge the digital divide, particularly by expanding connectivity to underserved communities.
From compliance to collaboration
A defining moment in Geetha's career came when she realised that technological success depends on more than innovation alone. It also requires alignment with policy, regulation and societal needs.
Her experience across spectrum, satellite and connectivity initiatives gradually transformed the way she viewed regulation.
"Instead of asking, 'How do we comply?', I began asking, 'How do we collaborate?'" she said.
The shift shaped her approach to regulatory affairs, placing greater emphasis on partnership, foresight and aligning business objectives with national digital ambitions.
For Geetha, regulation is not merely a framework that organisations must navigate. It is also a strategic enabler that can create the conditions for innovation, investment and long-term growth.
Securing critical resources
One of Geetha's most significant contributions has been advancing regulatory frameworks that safeguard satellite spectrum and orbital resources.

Through her work supporting Malaysia's positions at the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) World Radiocommunication Conference (WRC), she has contributed to efforts to secure access to resources that are critical to MEASAT's current and future satellite capabilities.

These resources underpin a range of connectivity services, including broadband access for rural and remote communities. They also support mobile backhaul that extends cellular coverage and provide resilient communications during emergencies.
For Geetha, the impact goes beyond technology.
"By securing access to these resources, MEASAT helps safeguard the connectivity that millions of Malaysians rely on every day," she said.
She believes these capabilities not only support digital inclusion but also strengthen Malaysia's digital sovereignty and communications resilience.
Regional leadership: Her work extends beyond Malaysia

Since 2016, she has chaired the Asia-Pacific Telecommunity's (APT) Drafting Group on Satellite Regulatory Matters and currently leads the Working Group on Space, Aeronautical and Maritime under APT's Wireless Group (AWG).

Through these leadership roles, she has helped shape regional policy discussions, build consensus among Asia-Pacific administrations, and advance regulatory frameworks that support innovation and digital connectivity across the region.

ac354197a442dc0c: PETALING JAYA: The Recording Industry Association of Malaysia (RIM) has defended the challenge by Public Performance Malaysia (PPM) and collective management organisations (CMO) against the Malaysian Intellectual Property Corporation's (MyIPO) copyright guidelines.
In a statement, RIM said PPM and the CMOs fully support any regulatory measure to enhance transparency and good governance for the benefit of creators.
"However, problematic provisions in the issued guidelines made it necessary for the CMOs to submit them to court for a judicial review," it said.
RIM declined to comment on the merits of the challenge while the matter remains before the courts.
"The existence of legal proceedings should not, in itself, be interpreted as evidence that an organisation opposes transparency or the protection of creators," it added.
RIM also denied the claim that PPM is its collection body, saying PPM is a separate entity with its own set of members and board of directors.
On Oct 7, the Malaysian Artistes’ Association (Karyawan) criticised RIM's call for funds to be set aside to promote Malaysian music internationally.

Karyawan said it was difficult to reconcile RIM’s request to the government for public funds with its move at the same time to contest the copyright guidelines. Karyawan also said RIM, through PPM as its collection body, along with two other CMOs, were challenging the guidelines in court.
RIM chairman Rosmin Hashim previously called on the government to establish a dedicated fund under the 2027 budget "to propel local music onto the global stage".

However, Karyawan said the industry’s problem was not a lack of funding but accountability, with artistes continuing to raise concerns over delayed royalty payments and a lack of transparency in how collections are calculated and distributed.
RIM said concerns over individual artiste's royalty payments should be investigated separately and not taken as proof that the entire system lacks transparency.

RIM said its call for a dedicated music fund is intended to support international showcases, overseas promotion, digital marketing and collaborations that can help Malaysian artistes and music companies access new markets.
"The focus should therefore be on ensuring that funding is properly implemented and delivers measurable benefits, rather than presenting investment and accountability as competing priorities.

"This proposal does not replace domestic market development; it complements it," RIM said, responding to Karyawan's claim that it is premature to talk about global expansion if Malaysian music does not have a strong presence in its own home market.

RIM also said it does not agree that domestic promotion must be completed before international promotion can begin, arguing that both are necessary and complementary to the long-term development of the music industry.
It said Japan and South Korea are examples of how sustained investment in talent, production and promotion can boost domestic demand and expand access to international markets.
6eebeb673cae7fb3: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Datuk Seri Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz today hailed private information platform aseanX as a potentially vital tool for deeper regional integration, as South-east Asian nations continue working to unlock Asean’s full economic potential.

48c477fc4aba1410: The prime minister has a once-in-a-generation chance to reintroduce compassion to welfare. 695c2f754208d78c: IPOH, Oct 16 — Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris (UPSI) and HONOR Technology (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd have signed a memorandum of agreement (MoA) to establish the HONOR AI Lab @ UPSI, aimed at strengthening education, research and innovation in artificial intelligence (AI).

UPSI Vice-Chancellor Prof Datuk Md Amin Md Taff and HONOR Malaysia CEO Ethan Chen signed the MoA at a ceremony witnessed by Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir at the main guest room of Dewan Tuanku Canselor, UPSI’s Sultan Azlan Shah Campus in Tanjong Malim on Wednesday.
Md Amin said establishing the lab is a strategic step to expand access to AI technology and provide university members with industry-based learning opportunities.

He said the HONOR AI Lab @ UPSI will not only provide a platform for students to explore AI technology, but also enable lecturers and researchers to expand their research and develop innovations relevant to the needs of the country’s digital economy.
“The collaboration allows the UPSI community to gain hands-on experience with advances in AI technology, narrowing the gap between classroom theory and its practical application in industry.

“The facilities and programmes will help students develop their technical competencies and soft skills, while giving lecturers opportunities to improve their teaching and research through the application of AI technology,” he said in a statement released by UPSI tonight.

Md Amin said the lab will serve as a hub for various AI-related activities, including workshops, professional certification programmes, student mobility opportunities, industrial training, innovation competitions and knowledge-sharing sessions with industry players.

Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir views a demonstration related to the HONOR AI Lab @ UPSI during the launch event at the university’s Sultan Azlan Shah Campus in Tanjong Malim. — Picture courtesy of HONOR Malaysia

He said that, to strengthen academic and research capabilities, UPSI lecturers also have access to industry-standard AI computing equipment, development tools and supporting hardware to facilitate the integration of AI applications into the curriculum and the implementation of research and innovation projects.
“The facility is also expected to foster collaboration between academics and industry experts to explore advances in AI technology and develop solutions that address current needs,” he said.

Meanwhile, Md Amin said UPSI students can take part in project-based learning activities, innovation competitions, mobility programmes and industrial training to gain greater practical exposure to AI technology.

“The professional certification programmes will also enable students to develop technical competencies and entrepreneurial skills in line with national competency standards, enhancing graduates’ employability in an increasingly technology-driven job market,” he said.

Meanwhile, Chen said the collaboration with UPSI underscores HONOR’s commitment to expanding access to the AI ecosystem and developing local talent to meet the needs of the rapidly growing technology industry.
“HONOR is committed to making the AI ecosystem accessible to all users, and this partnership with UPSI is an important step towards empowering the next generation of Malaysian talent.
“By breaking down industry barriers and working closely with academia, we hope to build a value-sharing ecosystem that benefits students, researchers and the wider community,” he said.
The two-year agreement provides for the HONOR AI Lab to be located at Tuanku Bainun Library, owned and managed by UPSI’s Faculty of Computing and Meta-Technology (FKMT). — Bernama

52c2044517097062: JAKARTA: Four men have died fighting wildfires in a national park on Indonesia's Java island, the forestry ministry said Friday, as the southeast Asian country battles a months-long crisis of blazes and toxic smoke.
The four were overwhelmed while battling flames Thursday in the Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park in East Java, a ministry statement said, without providing details on who the individuals were.
Two of the fallen men were national park officers, and two were security guards helping them, according to national park spokesman Endrip Wahyutama.
They had been trapped by flames and thick smoke. Three died at the scene, and a fourth later in hospital.
A volunteer firefighter and a security guard from a nearby hotel who also jumped in to help were receiving medical treatment, said Endrip.
A volunteer firefighter and a security guard from a nearby hotel who also jumped in to help were receiving medical treatment.
"This incident serves as a reminder that forest and land fire extinguishing is a high-risk operation," said the ministry.
It said there had been a jump in hotspots detected by satellites as areas of unusually high temperatures but did not necessarily translate into individual fires.
By Thursday evening, the number of hotspots stood at 799 nationally, up from 372 a day earlier.
Most were in Central Kalimantan, a province on Borneo Island that Indonesia shares with Malaysia and Brunei, followed by the south of Sumatra Island.
"Central Kalimantan recorded the largest increase (in hotspots), so field operations are being strengthened," said the statement.
The ministry expressed particular concern about an area around the Tanjung Puting National Park, an important habitat for endangered orangutans.
Water-bombing and cloud-seeding operations to make rain have been hampered by low visibility due to smoke from the fires, it added.

The ministry said several locations in Sumatra and Kalimantan were experiencing "unhealthy to very unhealthy conditions, even locally hazardous" due to the haze emitted by the blazes, turning the sky in some areas orange.
"If air conditions worsen, people are advised to reduce outdoor activities and wear masks when outside," it said.

fa4a29e715e9aac0: BEIJING: Some of China's richest people are winding down their offshore trusts, selling shares, and even switching nationality as a deadline looms to declare income booked overseas, say wealth advisers, lawyers and others familiar with the matter.

The move is part of tougher scrutiny of capital outflows and rule enforcement amid growing fiscal strains as the world's second-largest economy battles with persistent weakness in domestic demand and broader economic imbalances.

At the same time, tax officials have also stepped up efforts to gather information on wealthy individuals in their jurisdictions and are setting up dedicated teams to scoop up taxes owed on offshore incomes, they said.

Founders of Hong Kong- and US-listed Chinese firms would be hit the hardest in the latest tax move, as many of them sold shares through trusts at peak valuations between 2014 and 2020, said Oscar Liu, CEO of wealth adviser JLT Legacy Group.
"We estimate that the tax payable in a single case could range from a few million yuan to hundreds of millions, or even billions," said Liu, whose firm has offices in Hong Kong and Singapore.

In late July, Beijing set an Oct 22 deadline for the declaration of offshore trust income, with a tax of 20% to be imposed on such profits, triggering a scramble among wealthy Chinese individuals to tot up liabilities.

Boston Consulting Group estimates China's offshore wealth at about US$1.7 trillion, and offshore trusts have ⁠gained popularity in recent years as a tool for top shareholders of overseas-listed ​Chinese companies to park wealth outside the country.

China's State Taxation Administration has ordered employees to chase up those liable for offshore trust tax, working from a list drawn from the Hurun wealth rankings, corporate filings and other public information, three people said.
The people, who have knowledge of the matter, sought anonymity as the measures are confidential.
Taxmen in some provinces and cities with numerous wealthy entrepreneurs have set up special task forces dedicated to gathering information on offshore trusts, Liu added.
China's State Council, or cabinet, declined to respond to a Reuters request for comment. The State Taxation Administration and the finance ministry did not respond to requests for comments.
Finding Cash
The unexpected trust tax move has spurred a dash for cash in some cases.

A family office lawyer said clients cannot offset share-price losses against tax bills, while property developers who received large dividends in past years are now too weak financially to pay what they owe, as real estate languishes.
A tech billionaire's family office said it now spends more time calculating tax than trading and is selling about half its equity portfolio.
"It is like pulling the rug from under one's feet," said a person working there, referring to the demand to pay in cash within three months.

Banks are now lending to private clients to cover tax bills, with the loans secured against shares in the clients' own companies, said a private banker with a major international bank who deals with high net worth individuals and family offices.

China's offshore trust tax regime has also forced some of its wealthy to restructure businesses and family wealth holdings. Some have even shut newly established trusts before funding them, said one trust lawyer in Hong Kong.

A mainlander with Hong Kong citizenship, now working as an insurance agent in the Asian financial hub, said she was giving up her mainland residency to keep her husband's wealth out of Beijing's reach, even though he is not a mainland tax resident.
JLT's Liu said few offshore trust holders would rush into new investments, as they calculated tax liabilities.
Lack of clarity

Even those of China's wealthy who have started looking for options to pay taxes are confused by some aspects of the new rules that are unclear, from coverage targets and retroactive application to payment logistics.
"The net is very wide," said Wei Kang, a partner at law firm Charles Russell Speechlys who advises high-net-worth individuals and families on complex trust and estate structures, tax and compliance.

July's new tax rule ties liability to whether a taxpayer's "principal economic interest" lies in China, a concept open to interpretation that may not easily be settled by physical presence or citizenship, Kang added.
It is also unclear whether tax applies from the time a trust is set up, or for a limited period, she said.

The new rules also require those with offshore trust income to submit their own calculation of tax due by the Oct 22 deadline, and pay once authorities confirm the figure, said JLT Legacy Group's Liu.

In practice, however, enforcement varies by city with room in some cases for negotiation on repayment, seven people said. There is also no clear limit on how far back tax liability on dividends or share sales stretches, said three people.
"The devil is in the detail," Kang said. "A lot of details are lacking."
a86b4035cb33042c: BANGKOK: US Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh said Friday that AI technology was the "most consequential change" to the global economy he had seen, predicting its effects would be positive but the path forward would be "bumpy".

"I'd say the advent of this new technology is probably the most consequential change to the US and the global economy in my lifetime," he told an event at the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok.

Warsh said he takes the macroeconomic implications of the technology -- including a short-term driving of inflation through demand-side effects and an expected positive supply-side shock in the long term -- "soberly, responsibly" in his role as head of the US central bank.
He conceded that the AI investment boom would drive prices up in the short term, but "there really is, I think, a huge benefit to the global economy, to the US economy over the horizon".
He said he expected the Fed to use AI to be able to better analyse data in its conduct of monetary policy, as an example of the positive effects.
He also reiterated his previously stated belief that the technology would "make economies and countries that put it to good use more productive".
He cautioned, however, that the path forward was still laced with uncertainty about how markets would evolve around the technology.

"The path from where we are to there is likely to be a very bumpy one, bumpy in our understanding of the technology, bumpy because we really don't know what the market structure is going to be of these new technologies," he said.
95ca254acadbdb8f: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Malaysia’s economy expanded by 5.3 per cent in the third quarter of 2026 (3Q 2026), after registering 6.0 per cent growth in the preceding quarter, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM).
Its advance gross domestic product (GDP) estimates for 3Q 2026 report said all economic sectors, except mining and quarrying, underpinned performance, while mining and quarrying contracted.
“Cumulatively, for the first three quarters of 2026, Malaysia’s economy registered growth of 5.5 per cent, higher than 4.8 per cent in 2025’s corresponding period,” it said in a statement today.

The services sector remained the main impetus of economic growth in 3Q 2026, recording a 5.4 per cent increase (2Q 2026: 5.9 per cent), driven by the wholesale and retail trade, information and communication, and finance and insurance sub-sectors.

The department said the manufacturing sector strengthened to 7.5 per cent (2Q 2026: 7.3 per cent), backed by export-oriented industries, particularly electrical, electronic and optical products and petroleum, chemicals, rubber and plastics products.

“The construction sector grew by 6.0 per cent against 6.5 per cent in the preceding quarter, supported by the non-residential buildings sub-sector, particularly data centre construction projects, and specialised construction activities.
“The agriculture sector rebounded to 1.3 per cent (2Q 2026: -3.7 per cent), driven by oil palm and livestock sub-sectors,” it said.
The mining and quarrying sector, however, contracted by 4.9 per cent (2Q 2026: 9.2 per cent), due to a decline in the crude oil and condensate sub-sector.
It said the preliminary GDP, which provides a detailed and comprehensive analysis of economic performance for 3Q 2026, will be released on Nov 18, 2026. — Bernama

5dfd1577ababca43: PETALING JAYA: Adun Permatang Nurul Syazwani Noh mendedahkan beliau menerima surat tunjuk sebab daripada Bersatu berhubung kehadirannya pada Perhimpunan Agung Umno (PAU) 2026, 11 Sept lalu.
Menurut Syazwani, surat itu mengaitkan kehadirannya pada perhimpunan berkenaan dengan dakwaan melanggar etika dan tatakelakuan parti, termasuk tidak memelihara nama baik serta maruah Bersatu.

Syazwani yang juga ketua Bersatu Tanjong Karang berkata beliau sudah menjawab surat berkenaan dengan menjelaskan bahawa kehadirannya ke PAU adalah atas kapasiti peribadi dan bukan sebagai wakil parti.
“Saya pergi atas kapasiti peribadi, bukannya sebagai Adun Bersatu, delegasi atau mewakili Perikatan Nasional (PN). Saya hadir kerana menerima jemputan,” katanya dalam temu bual FMT.
Beliau berkata kini sedang menunggu keputusan berhubung surat tunjuk sebab itu.

Syazwani bagaimanapun tidak melihat kehadirannya ke PAU sebagai pelanggaran tatakelakuan kerana menurutnya, Bersatu tidak pernah mengeluarkan pekeliling yang melarang ahlinya menghadiri program anjuran parti politik lain.
Beliau turut merujuk keputusan Biro Politik Bersatu sebelum ini yang membenarkan Adun parti itu di Pahang memberikan sokongan kepada menteri besar daripada Umno, Ogos lalu.
Mereka adalah Adun Kuala Sentul Jasri Jamaluddin dan Adun Lepar Yazid Yunus.

“Jika sokongan politik sedemikian boleh diputuskan dan dibenarkan oleh parti, maka perlu dijelaskan bagaimana kehadiran saya ke PAU atas jemputan dan dalam kapasiti peribadi boleh dengan sendirinya dianggap mencemarkan nama baik atau maruah Bersatu,” katanya.
Syazwani turut mendakwa surat berkenaan mengandungi kesilapan fakta apabila menyatakan beliau sebagai ketua Bersatu Permatang sedangkan jawatannya adalah ketua Bersatu Tanjong Karang.
Beliau berkata sebarang tindakan disiplin perlu dilaksanakan mengikut perlembagaan dan prosedur parti, termasuk memaklumkan dengan jelas peruntukan yang didakwa telah dilanggar.

“Bagi saya, dalam apa-apa prosiding disiplin, seseorang ahli berhak mengetahui dengan jelas dan tepat apakah peruntukan yang dikatakan telah dilanggar serta apakah perbuatan tertentu yang membentuk kesalahan tersebut.
“Ini soal proses yang adil dan pematuhan kepada perlembagaan parti,” katanya.
Ditanya mengenai haluan politiknya, Syazwani berkata beliau belum menentukan “rumah perjuangan” seterusnya dan buat masa ini masih kekal sebagai ahli Bersatu.
Katanya, beliau juga mahu menghormati mandat yang diberikan pengundi kepadanya sebagai Adun Permatang.
“Saya menghormati mandat rakyat yang diberikan kepada saya sebagai Adun Permatang dan apa-apa keputusan mengenai masa depan politik saya hanya akan dibuat selepas pembubaran DUN Selangor,” katanya.
Pada 11 Sept lalu, Syazwani mencuri perhatian apabila hadir ke PAU dengan mengenakan pakaian menyerupai seragam Wanita Umno.
Kehadirannya berlaku ketika Umno giat mengetengahkan gagasan Rumah Bangsa yang antara lain bertujuan menyatukan orang Melayu serta membuka ruang kepada bekas ahli untuk kembali menyertai parti itu.
d95827e3d505fbad: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Debate on the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 was the main focus of the Dewan Rakyat in the second week of the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament, alongside current issues such as haze, health, education and school safety, as well as the cost of living.

A total of 75 government and opposition Members of Parliament (MPs) debated the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage over four days, beginning Monday (Oct 12), following the tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on October 9.

During the debate, Sabah and Sarawak MPs welcomed the increase in interim special grants to the two states from RM600 million to RM1.5 billion, but called for the final formula to be settled and for clarification on Sabah’s entitlement to 40 per cent of the federal government’s net revenue derived from the state.

Lim Guan Eng (PH-Bagan) proposed the permanent establishment of an Asean Special Task Force on Forest and Land Fires (Karhutla), involving Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines and Indonesia, to address the transboundary haze crisis. He also proposed legal action to claim compensation if Indonesia refused to accept the assistance.

Welfare issues also came under the spotlight, with Datuk Khlir Mohd Nor (PN-Ketereh) urging the government to expedite the resolution of pension adjustments for Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) veterans who retired before January 1, 2013.

Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor) stressed that school safety and bullying must not be taken lightly. He proposed a special allocation to train teachers to identify early signs of emotional distress and potential violence among students, while ensuring that every school had an adequate number of counsellors and structured psychological assessment programmes for early intervention.

During the oral question-and-answer session, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the procurement of 400 new ambulances would enhance emergency response capabilities for critical cases. He said his ministry had also increased medical equipment supplies to address the effects of haze, including 841 adult AeroChamber inhaler spacers, 396 units for children and 576 nebulisers.

Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the government aimed to create 500,000 job opportunities through initiatives involving artificial intelligence (AI), digitalisation and automation, while expanding high-growth, high-value industries and strategic sectors.

He said the government would also continue to stabilise the prices of essential goods through law enforcement, Jualan Rahmah Madani and Jualan Agro Madani, following the implementation of the RM2,000 minimum wage from June 2027.

Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said 1,726 private housing projects involving 199,643 units, with a gross development value of RM158 billion, had been successfully revived as of August through the efforts of the Task Force on Sick and Abandoned Private Housing Projects.

In the agriculture sector, Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the government would look into targeted assistance for paddy farmers who suffered lower yields due to delays in fertiliser supplies, to identify those who had genuinely incurred losses.

Meanwhile, the Minister’s Question Time (MQT) session on Tuesday, during which the Prime Minister is scheduled to answer questions raised by MPs, was answered by the relevant ministers as the Prime Minister was attending an event at Istana Negara.

During the Special Chamber session, Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said the transboundary haze, which had affected the country’s air quality since August 8, was expected to gradually subside over the next two weeks due to changing wind patterns during the monsoon transition period.

On Wednesday, the Dewan Rakyat also approved the appointment of four MPs — Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor), Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam), Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) and Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) — to the Parliamentary Services Council through a voice vote without debate.

The week’s sitting also saw the first reading of the Adoption (Amendment) Bill 2026 on Thursday, which, among other things, proposed amending Section 2 of Act 257 to redefine “child” by lowering the age limit from 21 to 18.
According to the Dewan Rakyat calendar, the policy-stage debate on Budget 2027 runs from October 12 to 22, followed by a four-day winding-up session by the relevant ministers beginning October 26.
The current Dewan Rakyat sitting will run for 37 days until December 8. — Bernama

6f6c01a258e60757: KUCHING, Oct 16 — Sarawak is exploring ways to improve healthcare delivery to remote communities following the suspension of its Flying Doctor Service (FDS) after a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Baram, that claimed five lives on September 8.

Deputy Minister of Public Health, Housing and Local Government Datuk Michael Tiang said alternative healthcare delivery methods would be used temporarily while the government formulates proposals to improve the service’s safety and effectiveness.

He said mobile clinic teams were being deployed via four-wheel-drive vehicles and boats to accessible areas, while emergency medical evacuations (Medevac) were being coordinated through alternative government air assets.
These include the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Air Unit, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Air Wing and the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF).

“The government will continue to evaluate and improve the methods of delivering healthcare services to rural areas, taking into account aspects of safety, effectiveness and service continuity, to ensure that rural communities continue to have access to the necessary healthcare services,” he said.
Tiang was responding to Krian assemblyman Friday Belik during the question-and-answer session at the State Legislative Assembly (DUN) sitting here on Friday.

He said the government was formulating proposals for a comprehensive improvement of the FDS, covering operational safety, aircraft suitability and capability, emergency training and preparedness, personnel welfare and protection, as well as alternative methods of delivering healthcare to rural communities.
The measures would take into account the findings of relevant assessments and investigations, as well as healthcare needs in remote localities.
Tiang also said the Sarawak State Health Department, in collaboration with JBPM, was organising the Sarawak Medevac Staff Engagement, Safety Briefing and Aircraft Familiarisation Roadshow 2026.

The initiative aims to strengthen medical personnel’s understanding, preparedness and confidence in Medevac operations and patient escorts to ensure evacuations are carried out safely and efficiently.

Tiang described the September 8 crash as a tragedy that deeply affected Sarawak, particularly the healthcare fraternity and the families of the five victims, comprising four healthcare personnel and a helicopter pilot.
He conveyed the Sarawak government’s condolences to the bereaved families and paid tribute to the victims for their service to communities in remote areas.
Introduced in Sarawak in 1973, the FDS provides primary healthcare, maternal and child health services, and emergency medical evacuations to communities inaccessible by road.
Tiang said the service had played an important role for decades in overcoming the geographical challenges faced by communities in Sarawak’s interior.
He stressed that the government would continue to assess appropriate service delivery methods to ensure healthcare access was maintained while prioritising safety and effectiveness. — The Borneo Post
